title: Human generation: high-likeness humanoid characters from a single portrait
body:
## Motivation

Today the character track is deliberately **stylized-only** — humans come out as game/figurine avatars, not photoreal likeness (a documented limit). The next leap for the project is turning a single portrait into a recognizable, animation-ready human.

## Scope

Wire the **projection-first likeness path** end to end into the character render:

- Solve the reference camera and camera-match the render (`scripts/solve_reference_camera.py`).
- De-light the photo to a neutral albedo before projection (`scripts/delight_reference.py`).
- Project the reference onto the fitted mesh (`scripts/bake_projected_texture.py`) using landmarks from `scripts/extract_reference_landmarks.py`.
- Report **per-region confidence** and request more views when a region is under-constrained.
- Stretch: a true humanoid rig (SkinnedMesh + morph targets) so the result can be posed/animated.

## Pointers

- `references/character-reconstruction.md`
- `references/likeness-maximization.md`
- `ROADMAP.md` (v1.3 Likeness maximization, v1.4 Animation-ready rigs)

## Acceptance criteria

- A real portrait photo produces a recognizable stylized-realistic human demo in the showcase.
- The pipeline emits a per-region confidence report and honestly flags low-confidence regions.
- No regression to the existing object/character pipelines.

**Difficulty:** hard · **Good for:** someone with 3D graphics / photogrammetry interest. Design discussion welcome before coding.

title: Auto-generate reference images from a text brief for real projects
body:
## Motivation

Right now you must hand the pipeline a reference image. For real projects you often start from a **text brief** or a partial asset list, not photos. An optional front-end that produces candidate reference images would let teams go from "I need a stylized loot chest" to a procedural Three.js model without sourcing art first.

## Scope

- An **opt-in, provider-agnostic** step: given a text prompt or a project/asset spec, generate or source candidate reference images, then feed the best one into the existing `probe → assessment → spec → generate` flow.
- Keep it pluggable — the image source (a text-to-image model, an asset search, or a user folder) should be behind a small adapter, not hard-wired to one provider.
- Surface licensing/provenance of any sourced image so nothing unlicensed slips into a build.

## Acceptance criteria

- `--from-prompt "<description>"` (or equivalent) yields a candidate reference the current pipeline consumes unchanged.
- The adapter interface is documented so a contributor can add a new image source in one file.
- Provenance/licensing is recorded in the assessment artifact.

## Open questions (discussion welcome)

- Which providers to support first, and how to keep the core dependency-free?
- How to rank/choose among multiple candidates automatically vs. asking the user?

**Difficulty:** medium–hard · research-flavored. Comment with design ideas before implementing.

title: 3D-print export: image to printable model (STL/OBJ/glTF + print prep)
body:
## Motivation

img2threejs output is a procedural `THREE.Group` — great for the browser, but not directly printable. A single "image → printable 3D model" path would open the project to the maker / 3D-printing community.

## Scope

- Bake a generated `THREE.Group` into a single merged, **watertight** `BufferGeometry` and export **STL / OBJ / glTF**.
- Basic print-prep: manifold/normals check, a wall-thickness warning, and scale-to-mm with a target longest-edge.
- Note (honestly) where a single-image reconstruction leaves hidden faces mirrored/approximated — printability depends on it.

## Pointers

- `ROADMAP.md` (v1.4 — glTF export)
- `root.userData.sculptRuntime` exposes the node/collider hierarchy to walk during the bake.

## Acceptance criteria

- `export --format stl` (or equivalent) produces a sliceable STL for the loot-chest demo that loads clean in a slicer.
- A manifold check reports non-watertight geometry instead of silently exporting a broken mesh.
- Documented limits: which subjects print well vs. need manual repair.

**Difficulty:** medium–hard. A great fit for someone who prints — real-world test prints as PRs very welcome.

title: Measured token-cost benchmark to replace the estimates
body:
## Motivation

The numbers in `docs/TOKEN_COST.md` are honest **engineering estimates**, not a measurement. Replacing them with a reproducible benchmark makes the token-efficiency claim credible and lets us track regressions.

## Scope

- A harness that runs N full reconstructions (fixed reference set) and records **real model-token spend** per stage (assessment, spec, codegen, each render-review cycle).
- Emit a table + per-stage breakdown, and a delta vs. the previous run.
- Keep it deterministic where possible so results are comparable across runs.

## Pointers

- `docs/TOKEN_COST.md` (the estimate tables to replace)
- `ROADMAP.md` (v1.5 — "measured token-cost benchmark replacing the current estimates")

## Acceptance criteria

- `scripts/benchmark_token_cost.py` (pure-stdlib, matching the repo's zero-dep tooling) produces a measured cost table.
- `docs/TOKEN_COST.md` gains a "Measured" section alongside the estimates.

**Difficulty:** medium · **Labels:** good first issue for someone who wants to learn the pipeline end to end.

title: Community demo gallery: accept demos via PR (showcase on-ramp)
body:
## Motivation

The live gallery ([hoainho/img2threejs-showcase](https://github.com/hoainho/img2threejs-showcase)) is the strongest way to show what the skill can do. Making it **accept community demos via PR** turns visitors into contributors and grows the gallery for free.

## Scope

- Document a **one-file contribution flow**: drop a `createXModel.ts` factory under `src/demos/<id>/`, add one `registry.ts` entry, add a reference image.
- Add a PR template for new demos (subject, reference source/license, a screenshot).
- Add a CI check that the showcase **builds** and the new demo route renders headless, so a demo PR can't break the site.

## Acceptance criteria

- A "Add your own demo" section in the showcase README with copy-paste steps.
- A PR template under `.github/`.
- CI that fails a demo PR if `tsc`/`vite build` fails or the route throws.

## Pointers

- `ROADMAP.md` (v1.5 — expanded gallery accepting community demos)
- The showcase repo's `src/demos/registry.ts` is the single source of truth.

**Difficulty:** good first issue · a clean, self-contained contributor on-ramp.

title: More procedural material recipes (metal, car paint, glass, leather...)
body:
## Motivation

Material fidelity is the single biggest lever on how "real" a reconstruction looks, but the documented recipe library is still small. This is one of the most contributor-friendly ways to improve every future model at once.

## Scope

Add documented, parameterized **procedural material recipes** (independent PBR channels, no albedo aliased into roughness), each with a parameter table and a tiny demo:

- Brushed / anisotropic metal
- Automotive paint (clearcoat + metallic flake)
- Subsurface wax / candle
- Frosted / rough glass
- Worn leather
- Anodized aluminium

## Pointers

- The material/lighting realism rubric in `references/`
- `scripts/extract_reference_pbr.py` (reference-derived PBR evidence)

## Acceptance criteria

- Each recipe lands as a documented block with parameters + a minimal before/after render.
- Recipes use real, separable PBR channels and real lights.

**Difficulty:** good first issue · pick a single material and open a focused PR. Ideal first contribution.

title: Broaden host/agent coverage with screenshot/vision adapters
body:
## Motivation

The skill promises to be **agent-agnostic** (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode — "use whatever the host provides"). In practice the screenshot/vision + browser steps are the part most likely to differ per host. Solid adapters + docs would let more people run it on their stack.

## Scope

- A thin **host adapter** interface for the two host-provided capabilities the loop needs: read an image with vision, and capture a browser screenshot.
- Reference adapters: a Playwright/Chrome-DevTools MCP screenshot path and a "user-supplied screenshot" fallback.
- A short per-host setup doc (Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode) covering how each satisfies the loop.

## Acceptance criteria

- Running the render-review loop on a second host works with only an adapter swap — no core changes.
- `references/` (or a new `docs/HOSTS.md`) documents the adapter contract and the per-host setup.

## Pointers

- `SKILL.md` — the "agent vision" / "agent browser tool" abstraction the loop already assumes.

**Difficulty:** medium · great for someone who runs a non-Claude host and wants first-class support for it.

title: Fix generator bypass of sculpt review gates
body:
## Summary

- make `generate_threejs_factory.py` use the orchestrator's authoritative review-completion gate
- prevent manually edited screenshot-only review history from unlocking later sculpt passes
- keep valid, fully reviewed passes unlockable and update the lock guidance to mention the required visual comparison evidence

## Problem

The generator had a weaker local copy of `review_completes_pass`. A manually edited review entry with `action=continue` and only `visualEvidence.renderScreenshot` could unlock the next pass, even though `sculpt_pass_orchestrator.py` correctly rejected the same entry because it lacked a comparison image, an accepted AI vision score, and passing critical feature reviews.

## Verification

- Added a regression test and confirmed it failed before the fix because the generator returned exit code 0.
- Confirmed the regression test passes after delegating to the orchestrator gate.
- Confirmed a valid review created through `append_sculpt_review.py` still unlocks `structural-pass` generation.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -v` — 20 tests passed.
- `ruff check scripts/generate_threejs_factory.py scripts/tests/test_pipeline.py` — passed.
- `python3 -m compileall -q scripts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

title: refactor: restructure project layout ahead of the full harness rebuild
body: Renames scripts/ -> forge/ and references/ -> grimoire/, reorganizes both into pipeline-stage/functional subfolders, differentiates naming from the shared upstream lineage, and drops the stale PROMOTION.md. Verified via forge/tests/test_pipeline.py (19/19 pass) with zero broken references.

title: Feature request: support more subject domains beyond object/character/hybrid
body:
## Summary

Today the pipeline classifies every reference image into just **3 subject domains** via `objectClass.primaryDomain` — `object | character | hybrid` (see `forge/stage2_spec/new_sculpt_spec.py`). This one axis (the *subject/asset category*) is the main thing limiting what img2threejs can reconstruct. I'd like to request first-class support for **more subject domains**.

## Motivation

In the 3D/game/CGI industry the "subject" axis is normally split much finer than object vs character. Common named categories:

- **Creatures / animals** — organic anatomy, but not humanoid (routes differently from the `character` anatomy track)
- **Vehicles** — cars, ships, mechs; hard-surface + moving/rotating parts (wheels, turrets)
- **Environments / scenes / dioramas** — modular kits and props arranged into a small world
- **Terrain / landscapes** — heightmap-driven natural surfaces
- **Foliage / vegetation / trees** — instanced, wind-animatable geometry
- **Architecture-scale buildings** — grid/modular structures larger than a single prop

Right now these all get forced into `object` or `hybrid`, so the spec templates, component trees, build passes, and feature-review targets don't match the subject. `character` already proves the value of a dedicated track (anatomy-aware componentTree, materials, passes in `make_character_*`). Each new domain would benefit from the same treatment.

## Proposal

1. Extend `objectClass.primaryDomain` beyond `object | character | hybrid` with a small, well-defined set (e.g. `creature`, `vehicle`, `environment`, `terrain`, `foliage`).
2. For each new domain, add a domain-specific track analogous to the existing character one:
   - a starter `componentTree` template,
   - default materials + build passes,
   - `featureReviewTargets` tuned to that subject,
   - a `grimoire/` rulebook page (mirrors `grimoire/character/reconstruction.md`).
3. Keep the strict-quality gate: a domain hint should still require the detail inventory + spec depth to pass.

## Non-goals

- No change to the geometry approach — output stays **procedural, code-generated Three.js** (that's the project's core value, not up for change).
- Not asking to drop the object/character/hybrid buckets, only to add alongside them.

## Open questions

- Which domains are highest priority? (My guess: `vehicle` and `environment/diorama` given the existing hard-surface strength.)
- Should some of these be a `primaryDomain` value vs. a modifier on top of `object`?

---
*Context: taxonomy compiled from industry sources (hard-surface vs organic modeling, standard asset categories). Happy to help draft the grimoire pages / spec templates if this is accepted.*

title: Feature request: optional explicit output-style mode (low-poly / anime-cel / PBR / voxel)
body:
## Summary

img2threejs currently infers the visual style purely from the reference image (`new_sculpt_spec.py` even notes *"Do not use fixed domain profiles"*). I'd like to request an **optional, explicit output-style mode** so a user can steer the reconstruction toward a chosen art style instead of relying only on inference.

## Motivation

In common usage, "types of 3D" most often refers to the **art-style axis**, and it's orthogonal to the subject axis. The standard named styles:

- **PBR / photorealistic** — physically-based materials, real light response
- **Low-poly** — intentionally limited polygon count, faceted/retro look
- **Voxel** — built from cubes
- **Anime / cel-shaded** — flat color regions + hard-edged shadows (toon shading)
- **Hand-painted / stylized** — lighting baked into albedo, non-PBR

The same reference image could legitimately be reconstructed as realistic *or* low-poly *or* cel-shaded depending on the target project. Inference alone can't disambiguate intent, and the choice drives very different decisions in the material-pass, surface-pass, and lighting-pass.

## Proposal

Add an optional `styleMode` to the spec (default: `auto` = today's in-image inference, so existing behavior is unchanged), e.g.:

```
styleMode: auto | pbr-realistic | low-poly | voxel | anime-cel | hand-painted
```

When set, it would:
- select a matching material strategy in the **material-pass** (e.g. `MeshToonMaterial` + banded lighting for `anime-cel`; flat-shaded reduced geometry for `low-poly`),
- adjust the **surface-pass / lighting-pass** acceptance criteria to the style,
- keep the vision-review gate, but score against the chosen style rather than photoreal fidelity.

## Non-goals

- `auto` stays the default — this is additive and opt-in.
- Not a full shader library; start with the 3–4 highest-value modes (`low-poly`, `anime-cel`, `pbr-realistic`).

## Open questions

- Should `styleMode` be a CLI/skill argument on invocation, or a field the agent fills during pre-spec assessment?
- Interaction with the existing per-feature quality thresholds — do they get relaxed for stylized modes?

---
*Related: subject-domain expansion request (separate issue). This one is the style axis; that one is the subject axis.*

title: Feature request: CS2 / Steam item reconstruction — data-driven finishes (paint kit, float, paint seed, Doppler)
body:
## Summary

Request a dedicated **Steam / CS2 item reconstruction track**. The repo already reconstructs weapons well (see the ISSACA shotgun and Gerber knife demos), so CS2 items look like a natural next subject. But CS2 skins are a special case: **they cannot be reconstructed correctly from a single 2D reference image alone**, which is exactly the current pipeline's only input. This issue proposes a **data-driven** finish path so the output actually matches the real item.

## The core problem (why image-only fails)

A CS2 skin's appearance is a *deterministic function of structured data*, not something recoverable from one flat icon:

- **Base weapon geometry** (fixed per weapon) + **paint kit** applied on top via a specific **finish style**.
- **Finish style** (the pipeline differs completely per style):
  1. Solid Color
  2. Hydrographic / Anodized
  3. Spray-Paint
  4. Anodized Multicolored (e.g. **Doppler**)
  5. Custom Paint Job (non-tiled illustrative texture, peels to substrate)
  6. Patina / Antiqued (oxidation: darkens + hue-shifts with float, doesn't scratch)
  7. Gunsmith (hybrid mask of custom-paint + patina)
- **Float / wear value** (FN→BS): drives a *wearness mask stored in the albedo alpha channel* (~196 = erodes early, <128 = durable, 0 = never erodes), plus AO/curvature maps that concentrate scratches on sharp edges.
- **Pattern index / paint seed** (1–1000): initializes a deterministic generator that computes an **affine transform** (`A = T₂·R·S·T₁`) shifting the pattern/wear/grunge layers across the UVs. This is *why the same skin looks different per item* — Fade %, Case-Hardened blue, Doppler phase, "Max" patterns.
- **PBR metallic-roughness maps** (base color / roughness / normal / metalness — binary 0/1) that a 2D icon has flattened away.
- **HDR environment cubemap** — anodized/gem finishes get their shimmer from reflections; under flat lighting they look muddy and lifeless.

A Steam Market icon is a generic flat render with none of this: no paint seed, no PBR maps, no view-dependent behavior.

## Concrete failure case: Doppler knife

I tried reconstructing a **Doppler knife** and it didn't look right — this is the canonical example of why:

- Doppler is **Anodized Multicolored**: a black/silver **marbleizing** base + a translucent **candy-coat gradient** + **view-dependent iridescence** (Black Pearl shifts purple↔green with angle).
- **Phase** (Phase 1–4, Ruby, Sapphire, Black Pearl) is not in the image — it's tied to the paint seed / pattern.
- The color comes from **HDR cubemap reflections**, so a flat-lit reconstruction from one 2D frame is inevitably muddy and off.

To render it correctly you need: metalness 0.90–1.00, roughness 0.05–0.15, `envMapIntensity` 1.5–2.5, a real HDRI env map, the affine UV transform from the paint seed, and filmic (ACES-like) tonemapping in sRGB.

## Proposal

Add a CS2/Steam-item track that is **data-driven, not image-only**:

1. Accept structured inputs alongside (or instead of) the reference image:
   `weapon`, `paintKit`, `finishStyle` (enum above), `float`, `paintSeed`, optional StatTrak / nametag / charm.
2. Build the finish **procedurally per finish-style pipeline** rather than trying to paint the observed icon onto the mesh.
3. Make an **HDRI environment map mandatory** for anodized/gem finishes, with metallic-roughness PBR and filmic tonemapping — otherwise reject as "will look muddy".
4. Drive wear from the **float → wearness-mask** model, and pattern placement from the **paint-seed affine transform**.
5. Expose runtime hooks so the knife can be inspected/orbited (view-dependent finishes only read correctly in motion).

## Non-goals

- Not asking to abandon the image input — the reference image still guides base geometry / sanity-check. The ask is to *add* the structured finish data the image can't carry.
- Output stays procedural code-generated Three.js.

## Open questions

- Where do the structured attributes come from — user-supplied, or pulled from a source (e.g. inspect link / community pattern DB)?
- Should "CS2 item" be a new `objectClass.primaryDomain`, or a specialized profile layered on the existing hard-surface/weapon path?

---
*Technical requirements above compiled from prior CS2 rendering research (finish styles, float/wear masks, paint-seed affine transform, Source 2 PBR ranges, Doppler HDR dependence). Related: #10 (subject domains), #11 (style modes).*

title: Native GLB export from the viewer
body:
## Native GLB export from the viewer

Adds a decoupled browser module, `export/glbExporter.js`, that exports any img2threejs
procedural model to a Blender-ready `.glb` with one click — no build step, no npm
install, no pipeline coupling.

### What's included
- `export/glbExporter.js` — `exportModelToGLB(root, options)` (returns a Blob) and
  `attachExportButton(root, options)` (adds a floating "Exportar .glb" button). Wraps
  `three/addons/exporters/GLTFExporter.js`, resolved via the viewer importmap.
- `grimoire/export/glb_export.md` — integration + behavior docs.
- `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `ROADMAP.md` — export documented as a
  standard output step.

### Design notes
- Exports a **sanitized clone**: strips the circular `root.userData.sculptRuntime`
  graph (which would otherwise break cloning / bloat `extras`) while preserving node
  `.name` values, so the named hierarchy survives into Blender.
- `resetRootTransform` neutralizes the viewer's animated spin so it isn't baked in.
- Model only — scene lights are excluded.
- Standard PBR materials (`MeshStandardMaterial` / `MeshPhysicalMaterial`) and
  `CanvasTexture` export fully (clearcoat, emissive, transmission, baked canvas textures).

### Verification
Wired into a real viewer (Master Sword) and validated end-to-end: the exported `.glb`
has a correct binary header (`glTF`, version 2, JSON chunk), and its glTF contains the
expected meshes, materials, and named nodes (`blade`, `guard`, `grip`, `pommel`).

### Out of scope
Headless Node CLI export, material editing, and non-GLB formats (OBJ/FBX/USD).

title: v1.3: Upgrade quality and efficiency
body:
Changelog — v1.3

Added

* Reference-grounded gradient extraction — Gradients are now sampled directly from the reference image using band-median analysis, replacing manually guessed gradient stops. Also adds blue-collapse detection and magenta-lean hints for improved color fidelity.
* Candy-coat material model — Added support for dielectric candy/anodized/PVD-style finishes with tuned PBR parameters for richer, more accurate coatings. Includes automatic material classification (e.g. chrome → gem-metal, bright-clean → gemstone) and palette hue risk analysis.
* CIEDE2000 color metric — Introduced an accurate CIEDE2000 (ΔE00) implementation with sRGB → CIELAB conversion, validated against Sharma’s reference test pairs for perceptual color comparison.
* Divine Eye color diagnostics (report-only) — Added new analysis signals:
    * Hue Zone Parity detects hue shifts across gradient bands (e.g. purple drifting toward blue).
    * Specular Wash detects saturation loss and cyan drift caused by overly strong highlights.
        These metrics are currently informational only and do not affect validation scores while calibration is in progress.

Improved

* InstancedMesh rendering — Repeated geometry is now rendered using a single draw call for significantly better performance. Improved cluster resolution also eliminates previous base-geometry crashes.
* Ground blade UV mapping — UV generation now uses the true Y-span of the geometry, fixing edge clamping artifacts that previously caused flat colors and white tip issues.
* Cutout generation — Extrusion now supports Shape.holes and oval loop cutouts, enabling clean wire-cutter style holes without requiring CSG operations.

title: Proposal: x402 Payment Integration — let agents pay per 3D model, directly to you
body:
## Summary

You've built something valuable — an image-to-3D pipeline that should be an API, not just a CLI tool. Right now you rely on donations. This proposal shows you how to get paid **every time someone generates a 3D model**, without subscriptions, without a storefront, without leaving GitHub.

## The Gap

Your pipeline is useful for:
- Game devs who need quick 3D assets
- Web developers building Three.js scenes
- AI agents that need to generate 3D content autonomously

But none of them can pay you for it. Your donate link is generous, but donations don't scale.

## The Solution: x402

x402 (HTTP 402 Payment Required) lets you charge per model generation. The flow:

1. An agent or developer sends an image to your API
2. Your server responds with HTTP 402 + a payment challenge
3. The client signs a USDC payment proof (a few cents per model)
4. Your server verifies the payment and returns the Three.js code
5. You get paid instantly, no middleman

**Every model generation = revenue in your wallet.**

## Why This Fits img2threejs

| Feature | Today (Donations) | With x402 |
|---------|-------------------|-----------|
| Revenue | Sporadic, tiny % of users | Every commercial use pays |
| API access | CLI only, no API | Any agent can call it |
| Sustainability | Hobby project | Self-funding business |
| Distribution | GitHub stars | Agent discovery too |

**The market exists.** Game devs, web builders, and AI agents all need 3D assets. With x402, every single one of those use cases pays you directly.

## What I'm Offering

I maintain a production x402 gateway (16 endpoints, 5 chains, live on x402scan) and have contributed x402 integrations to GOAT AgentKit, Obsidian Mind, MiroFish, and Injective iAgent. I can:

1. Draft an x402 middleware module for your pipeline (Python — your stack)
2. Submit as a PR to your forge/ directory
3. Register it on the x402 ecosystem so agents discover it

## About Me

I'm the orchestrator of GenTech Labs — we help creators monetize their work. We're the monetization layer for the agent economy.

Would you be open to a PR?

title: Verified accuracy bugs: dead scale hard gate, color-blind fidelity score, unflagged mask inversion, silent fallback geometry, discarded anatomy data
body:
While studying how to improve reconstruction accuracy, I audited the review/scoring pipeline and intake scripts, then had each suspected issue independently re-verified (adversarially, with small stdlib repro scripts run against the actual modules — no repo modifications). Everything below is confirmed against current `main` (`7b1c62c`). Happy to split any of these into separate issues or send PRs.

## Confirmed bugs

### 1. The Divine Eye's scale hard gate can never fire (key-name mismatch)

`proportion_delta` returns snake_case keys (`forge/stage4_review/diagnose_render.py:114`):

```python
return {"aspect_ratio_delta": round(aspect_ratio_delta, 4), "scale_delta": round(scale_delta, 4)}
```

but `evaluate()` reads camelCase with silent `0.0` defaults (`forge/stage4_review/divine_eye.py:287-288`):

```python
scale_delta = prop.get("scaleDelta", 0.0)
aspect_delta = prop.get("aspectRatioDelta", 0.0)
```

Consequences:
- The `SCALE_HARD_MAX` hard gate (`divine_eye.py:329-330`) is dead code — one of only two hard gates.
- The `proportion` soft signal (`divine_eye.py:336`) is always exactly `1.0`, inflating every fidelity score.
- The objectness rescue at `divine_eye.py:369-373` promises it "never rescues a scale-delta failure" — but since scale-delta failures can't exist, a grossly mis-scaled render with high objectness can be rescued to `probe`.

**Repro:** reference 16×64 rect vs render 112×24 rect → true `scale_delta = 1.625` (threshold 0.08), yet `signals.scaleDelta = 0.0`, no hard-gate failure, proportion score `1.0`. (Tier-1 `run_tier1` at `diagnose_render.py:178-179` reads the correct keys, so only the Divine Eye is affected.)

### 2. Tiny-mask inversion reaches the Divine Eye's IoU unflagged — disjoint objects can score IoU 1.0

`build_foreground_mask` inverts to "all opaque pixels" when coverage < 3.5% (`forge/stage1_intake/extract_pbr_evidence.py:256-259`), signalled only via the warnings list. `diagnose_render_multi_angle.py:52-53` checks for that warning; the Divine Eye path discards it (`diagnose_render.py:66-67`: `mask, _diag, _warn = build_foreground_mask(...)`).

**Repro:** 200×200 white frames; reference = 30×30 red square top-left, render = 30×30 blue square bottom-right (each 2.25% coverage, zero silhouette overlap). Both masks invert to full-frame → `silhouetteIoU = 1.0`, no hard-gate failure, no flag anywhere in the output JSON. True IoU is 0.

### 3. Color is completely absent from the gated fidelity score

Every weighted signal in the ensemble (`divine_eye.py:335-346`) is luma- or shape-derived. `hueZoneParity` / `specularWash` (`divine_eye.py:316-323`) are report-only and affect neither fidelity, hard gates, nor routing.

**Repro:** identical shape/shading, red reference vs blue render → `verdict: pass, action: continue, fidelity: 0.9485` while `hueZoneParity` correctly reads `0.0` and is ignored. The only color gate anywhere is Tier-1's `per_part_color_delta`, which compares the render against the *spec recipe* (not the reference), uses CIE76, and only fails at ΔE > 20 from `material-pass` onward (`diagnose_render.py:201-208`). A full CIEDE2000 implementation already exists in `forge/_shared/color_metrics.py` — it's just not in the weighted score.

### 4. Missing lathe/extrude/tube profiles silently render hardcoded default shapes

`geometry_for` substitutes `_DEFAULT_LATHE_PROFILE` / `_DEFAULT_EXTRUDE_PROFILE` / `_DEFAULT_TUBE_PATH` when a descriptor omits its profile data (`forge/stage3_build/generate_threejs_factory.py:232-245, 279-291`) — no warning, no marker in the generated TS, exit 0. `validate_sculpt_spec.py` (including `--strict-quality`) never checks that a lathe/extrude/tube primitive carries profile data (`validate_geometry_descriptor`, `forge/stage2_spec/validate_sculpt_spec.py:509-531`). Worse, the flatness gate (`validate_sculpt_spec.py:88-110`) only fires when `profile2D` *is present*, so omitting the profile evades an existing quality gate.

This contradicts the generator's own `GeometryNotImplementedError` docstring four lines above the defaults ("Never silently substitute a box... with no signal that anything was wrong", `generate_threejs_factory.py:224-228`).

**Repro:** minimal spec with a lathe component and no `latheProfile` → validator passes clean, generator exits 0, output contains the default hourglass `[[0.3,-0.5],[0.15,0.0],[0.3,0.5]]` verbatim.

### 5. Character `anatomy` is measured, threaded through, and silently discarded

`make_character_component_tree(anatomy)` (`forge/stage2_spec/new_sculpt_spec.py:267`) accepts the anatomy dict extracted from the assessment (`new_sculpt_spec.py:1122-1126` → `apply_character_template` → line 390) and **never references the parameter in its body**. Every proportion is a hardcoded head-unit constant (`hu = 0.28`, lines 277-315).

**Repro:** passing an extreme filled anatomy (styleHeads 2.0, headUnit 0.5, shoulderWidth 3.0) produces a componentTree byte-identical to the no-anatomy tree. So even landmark proportions the agent measures per `extract_landmarks.py`'s instructions never reach the spec programmatically.

Related: the "generic" humanoid template is hardcoded to one specific dev subject — every character spec seeds with a `"Chest graphic (Orioles)"` decal, side-swept hair, glasses, and headphones (`new_sculpt_spec.py:280-296`), and `CHARACTER_MATERIALS` bakes that subject's palette (lines 334-344).

### 6. `derive_geometry.py` is orphaned, and its algorithm isn't what its docstring claims

- **Orphaned:** the only reference in the entire repo is `forge/tests/test_geometry_derivation.py`. It appears in neither `SKILL.md`'s workflow nor `grimoire/scripts.md` (the canonical script catalog), yet `CHANGELOG.md:16` advertises "Blum lathe-profile derivation" as shipped in v1.3. Nothing ever writes `latheProfile` into a spec, so the generator's only lathe input is agent-authored or the silent default from bug 4.
- **Mislabeled:** the docstring claims Blum-medial-axis inscribed half-width, but the implementation takes half the *outermost row span* (`derive_geometry.py:79`, `_row_span` at lines 29-38 ignores interior gaps). Repro: a two-lobe silhouette (two 11px bars, 60px gap) yields radius 0.4706 vs a true inscribed ~0.06; a hollow square frame produces a profile identical to a solid slab. The existing 5 tests pass because all fixtures are convex/single-span, which cannot distinguish the two algorithms.

### 7. White/near-white objects on white backgrounds are dropped by the foreground mask

The keying clause (`extract_pbr_evidence.py:254`) requires `distance > max(24, noise*2.4)` **or** (`sat > 0.16 and luma < 0.94`). A bright low-saturation object within RGB distance ~24 of the background fails both.

**Repro:** RGB(243,243,243) object filling 36% of a white frame → zero pixels keyed as foreground, then the <3.5%-coverage fallback swaps in the full frame (coverage reads 1.0), so palette/albedo evidence is dominated by background. RGB(230,230,230) works fine (distance 43). This is exactly the common "white product on white e-commerce background" reference style.

### 8. Empty-union comparisons return perfect scores

`silhouette_iou` (`diagnose_render.py:85`) and `edge_overlap` (`divine_eye.py:236`) both return `1.0` when the union is empty, with no caller guard. Scope is narrow — it needs *both* masks empty (e.g. two failed captures) — and in that case the Eye currently lands on `probe` only by accident of the disagreement-spread heuristic, not by any guard. Returning 0.0 / an explicit invalid-mask verdict would be safer.

### 9. Image decoding portability

`load_image`'s only non-PNG path shells out to macOS `sips` (`extract_pbr_evidence.py:189-207`), so JPEG references fail hard on Linux/Windows (`ValueError ... sips is unavailable`). Additionally, 16-bit and interlaced PNGs fail **even on macOS**, because sips's png→png conversion preserves the offending encoding and `read_png` (line 103) rejects it again. The same sips-only pattern is duplicated in `extract_landmarks.py:166`, `delight_albedo.py:164`, `build_detail_inventory.py:147`, and `make_comparison_sheet.py:131`.

### 10. Correction loop: two reverts are permanently sticky (possibly intended, worth a look)

`correction_loop.py:79` counts reverts over the **entire** history (`oscillating = reverts >= 2`), while the direction-flip check only inspects the last 3 entries (lines 81-87). Two early, already-recovered reverts route every subsequent `decide()` to `refine-spec` forever — verified with a synthetic history of 2 reverts followed by 6 strictly improving clean passes. The cumulative threshold is unit-tested (`test_correction_loop.py`), so it may be a deliberate conservative rule, but the permanent stickiness across a refine-spec cycle (nothing documents that history resets) and the inconsistent windows look like unexamined consequences.

## Smaller signal-quality gaps (all verified, all self-documented as deferred)

- `global_ssim` is a single window over the whole 64×64 luma image (`divine_eye.py:199-212`) — one global covariance number, not windowed SSIM.
- Edge overlap is exact per-pixel IoU with zero misalignment tolerance (`divine_eye.py:215-236`); a ~3px shift at full res drops it from 1.0 to ~0.59. (Chamfer matching is already noted as deferred in the module docstring.)
- Nearest-neighbor point sampling in `load_mask` (`diagnose_render.py:64-74`), `objectness._resample_bbox` (`objectness.py:61-72`), and `make_comparison_sheet.resize_cover` (lines 158-176) aliases thin features. (`divine_eye.load_luma` is properly box-averaged, so the SSIM/tonal path is fine.)
- `diagnose_render_multi_angle.py` is mandated by SKILL.md but not enforced anywhere in code — unlike Tier-1, which `orchestrate_passes.py check` refuses without. Its only importer is its own test.
- `vlm_gate.py` has no sampler implementation anywhere in the repo, and the real review path (`append_review.py --ai-vision-score`) never invokes `gate()`; `calibrate_eye.py` requires a labeled corpus that doesn't exist, so all the fixed thresholds (IoU 0.85, Sobel 0.12, blowout ×4, ...) are uncalibrated.

## Suggested priority

Bugs 1–3 mean the automated review loop currently approves renders it is designed to reject (wrong scale, disjoint silhouettes, wrong colors). They're also the smallest diffs: fix the two key names, propagate mask warnings into `evaluate()`, and add a zoned ΔE signal using the CIEDE2000 code already in `_shared/color_metrics.py`. Bugs 4–5 are the highest-leverage accuracy fixes on the generation side.

I have minimal repro scripts for each confirmed item and am glad to contribute PRs for any of them.

Native GLB export from the viewer (rebase of #13)
body:
Rebased continuation of #13 by @juancamusss, which is currently marked CONFLICTING against `main` after the v1.3 (#14), Apache-2.0 relicense (#16), and star-history (#20) merges. All original commits are cherry-picked with authorship preserved; the only conflict was CHANGELOG section ordering (the new `[Unreleased]` block now sits above `[1.3.0]`). One commit is added on top updating the `docs/UPGRADE_PLAN.md` status line, per CONTRIBUTING.md ("update UPGRADE_PLAN status when you land a roadmap item").

If @juancamusss rebases #13 directly, feel free to close this one.

---

## Native GLB export from the viewer

Adds a decoupled browser module, `export/glbExporter.js`, that exports any img2threejs
procedural model to a Blender-ready `.glb` with one click — no build step, no npm
install, no pipeline coupling.

### What's included
- `export/glbExporter.js` — `exportModelToGLB(root, options)` (returns a Blob) and
  `attachExportButton(root, options)` (adds a floating "Exportar .glb" button). Wraps
  `three/addons/exporters/GLTFExporter.js`, resolved via the viewer importmap.
- `grimoire/export/glb_export.md` — integration + behavior docs.
- `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `docs/UPGRADE_PLAN.md` —
  export documented as a standard output step.

### Design notes
- Exports a **sanitized clone**: strips the circular `root.userData.sculptRuntime`
  graph (which would otherwise break cloning / bloat `extras`) while preserving node
  `.name` values, so the named hierarchy survives into Blender.
- `resetRootTransform` neutralizes the viewer's animated spin so it isn't baked in.
- Model only — scene lights are excluded.
- Standard PBR materials (`MeshStandardMaterial` / `MeshPhysicalMaterial`) and
  `CanvasTexture` export fully (clearcoat, emissive, transmission, baked canvas textures).

### Verification
- Wired into a real viewer and validated end-to-end: the exported `.glb` has a correct
  binary header (`glTF`, version 2, JSON chunk) and contains the expected meshes,
  materials, and named nodes.
- All 20 forge test suites pass on this rebased branch (`python3 forge/tests/test_*.py`),
  including `test_pipeline.py` (42/42).

### Out of scope
Headless Node CLI export, material editing, and non-GLB formats (OBJ/FBX/USD).

title: Add procedural demon bear 3D character model
body:
## 概述

將風格化 2D 惡魔熊角色設計轉換為完整的 Three.js 3D 模型。這是 img2threejs 專案的首次角色模型演示，展示了從參考圖像到程序化 3D 重建的完整工作流程。

## 實現內容

### 核心 3D 模型 (`src/createDemonBearModel.ts`)
- **30+ 程序化組件**：身體、頭部、雙臂、雙腿、尾巴、爪子、縫線細節
- **精確比例**：根據參考圖像的風格化特徵（頭部約為身體高度的 1/3）
- **非對稱姿態**：左臂抬起、右臂下垂，捕捉兇悍的姿態
- **PBR 物理材質系統**：
  - 黑色主體（粗糙度 0.7）
  - 紅色發光眼睛和 X 標記（含自發光）
  - 白色縫線細節
  - 膚色爪子

### 動畫系統
- 頭部搖擺（±0.1 單位）
- 尾巴擺動（±0.2 弧度）
- 呼吸效果（±5% 垂直縮放）
- 可配置的動畫速度

### 互動式 3D 檢視器 (`index.html`)
- 實時 WebGL 渲染
- 滑鼠互動視角控制
- 專業光影設置（環境光 + 方向光 + 點光源）
- 即時 FPS 和統計數據顯示
- 響應式設計，支援所有螢幕尺寸

### 完整文檔 (`DEMON_BEAR_README.md`)
- 使用指南和 API 文檔
- 完整組件層級說明
- 材質和光照推薦設置
- 效能特性和優化建議

## 技術細節

**模型統計：**
- 多邊形數：~15,000 三角形
- 材質數：4 種
- 幾何類型：Sphere、Cylinder、Box、Cone（廣泛相容）
- 動畫類型：變形動畫（非骨骼綁定）

**相容性：**
- Three.js r128+
- 所有現代瀏覽器（Chrome、Firefox、Safari、Edge）
- 適合行動裝置和網頁應用

## 特點亮點

✅ 完全程序化構建（無 mesh 檔案或模型匯入）  
✅ 從 2D 參考精確重建的風格化特徵  
✅ 即用型動畫系統  
✅ 運行時可定製（暴露組件層級和參數）  
✅ 低多邊形且效能友善  
✅ 完整的 TypeScript 類型定義

## 使用示例

```typescript
import { createDemonBearModel, animateDemonBear } from './src/createDemonBearModel';

const model = createDemonBearModel({ scale: 1.5, animationSpeed: 1 });
scene.add(model);

// 在動畫循環中
function animate(time) {
  animateDemonBear(model, time);
  renderer.render(scene, camera);
}
```

或直接在瀏覽器中開啟 `index.html` 查看互動式演示。

## 檔案結構

```
.
├── src/createDemonBearModel.ts       # TypeScript 模型工廠
├── examples/demonBearDemo.ts         # 完整場景範例
├── index.html                         # 互動式檢視器（開箱即用）
├── DEMON_BEAR_README.md              # 詳細文檔
├── assets/
│   ├── character-demon-bear.jpg      # 原始參考圖像
│   ├── character-demon-bear.png      # PNG 版本
│   └── character-demon-bear-zones/   # 區域分析圖
├── character-assessment.json         # 預規格評估
└── detail-inventory.json             # 詳細庫存
```

## 測試方法

1. 在現代瀏覽器中開啟 `index.html`
2. 移動滑鼠環繞 3D 模型
3. 觀察流暢的動畫效果
4. 查看 FPS 和統計資訊

## 後續改進方向

- [ ] 骨骼綁定支援（v1.4 路線圖）
- [ ] 形態目標（面部表情）
- [ ] glTF/FBX 導出
- [ ] 碰撞形狀和物理集成
- [ ] 其他角色和動畫變體

title: Rewrite roadmap: one theme per release, v1.4 Weapon through v2.0 Procedural World
body:
Docs only: a themed roadmap, a fuller shipped history, a stronger prompt example, and links pointed at the org's canonical URLs.

## `ROADMAP.md` — rewritten

- **Shipped** section now records the real history with dates, and expands **v1.2** and **v1.3** into their full changelog detail rather than a one-line summary.
- Corrects a factual error: v1.3 was labelled *"likeness maximization"*; the shipped 1.3.0 release is **quality & efficiency (Divine Eye)** — the deterministic review harness, input-integrity and geometry-truth gates, texture/gradient analysis, CIEDE2000 colour math.
- New themed roadmap **v1.4 → v2.0**, each release with a goal, highlights, a per-version write-up, and a release name (The Weapon Update, The Character Update, …).
- Four-phase long view: assets → worlds → production → AI game-asset platform.
- **Known gaps** re-mapped onto the new numbering instead of pointing at the old versions: G1 (SkinnedMesh / morph targets) → v1.8, G2 (glTF export) → v1.7, G4 (baking / LOD) → v1.7, G6 (retopology) → feeds v1.5. G3 stays flagged as the one real latent bug.
- No emoji.

## `README.md` — additive only

Nothing is removed; three areas are updated in place.

- **`## Roadmap`** — keeps the existing bullet-list shape. The shipped bullets stay (v1.3 corrected), the upcoming themed releases are added, and the section now points clearly into `ROADMAP.md` for the full detail.
- **Quick start** — the one-line prompt stays as the entry point. A new **"Driving it harder"** subsection adds an advanced prompt whose every line maps onto a real gate or artifact (detail inventory, reference-derived finish class and gradient stops, runtime pivots/sockets/`userData.tick`, `--strict-quality`, per-region confidence), plus per-subject variants for likeness, creatures, candy-coat finishes, and a cost ceiling.
- **Links** — `github.com/hoainho/img2threejs*` → `github.com/img2threejs/img2threejs*` after the transfer to the org, and the retired `hoainho.github.io/img2threejs-showcase/` GitHub Pages URLs → `img2threejs-showcase.pages.dev`.

## Deliberately untouched

- **License.** The in-flight `feature/plan-1.3-quality-and-efficiency` branch relicenses Apache-2.0 → MIT. That is a separate decision and is **not** in this PR — the license badge and license section here are byte-identical to `main`.
- **Star-history block.** Its chart URLs carry a `sealed_token` bound to the old repo path, so rewriting the `repos=` parameter would likely invalidate the chart. Left as-is; worth regenerating separately.
- **Version badge.** Still reads `1.2.0`, pending the re-tag below.

## Follow-up needed

The creature-generator tranche is shipped but tagged `1.4.0` in `CHANGELOG.md`, and `SKILL.md` reads `1.5.0`. Both need re-tagging onto a `1.3.x` line — otherwise readers see "v1.4 shipping soon" next to a shipped v1.4 changelog entry. `ROADMAP.md` carries a note about this.

title: Feat/add cs2 item reconstruction
Optimize Chrome Agent Usage to Reduce Unnecessary Token Consumption
body:
Problem

When running img2threejs with Chrome-based browser automation, a significant amount of tokens are spent on interactions that provide little or no value to the generation process.

Based on testing, approximately 50% of the total token usage is consumed by unnecessary browser context, repeated DOM extraction, verbose console logs, and redundant page state descriptions.

This increases both:

* API cost
* Generation latency

without improving output quality.

Proposed Improvements

* Minimize DOM/context sent to the LLM.
* Filter out irrelevant browser logs before passing them to the model.
* Avoid repeatedly reading unchanged page content.
* Cache browser state between verification steps.
* Only expose the information required for screenshot validation.
* Reduce verbose Chrome automation prompts.

Expected Result

* ~50% lower token consumption during browser-assisted verification.
* Faster generation.
* Lower API costs.
* No impact on model quality or verification accuracy.

Notes

This optimization should focus on reducing browser overhead rather than changing the core generation pipeline. The goal is to make Chrome act as a lightweight verification tool instead of continuously streaming large amounts of unnecessary context.

[Research] Intake tối giản hai ảnh và identity arbitration cho item CS2
body:
## Bối cảnh

Người dùng không nên phải viết prompt mô tả item dài. Intake mong muốn chỉ gồm:

```text
Ảnh trước: [img1]
Ảnh sau: [img2]
Tên item: [tuỳ chọn]
```

Pipeline phải tự phân tích cấu trúc, vật liệu, finish, chi tiết, phần suy luận và tạo prompt/spec nội bộ cho img2threejs.

## Research đã xác minh

- OpenSpec change `cs2-image-matched-3d-reconstruction` hiện hợp lệ, có đủ proposal/design/specs/tasks; task progress là 36/37 (còn calibration golden-render threshold).
- `cs2-intake.json` hiện chỉ nhận một source view với role `reference`; CLI cũng chỉ nhận một positional `reference`.
- Classification record hiện là đầu vào authoritative bắt buộc trước khi manifest chọn family adapter.
- `resolve_identity()` đang ưu tiên explicit user metadata trước resolved metadata và classification record. Điều này có thể ép ảnh vào tên item sai.
- BM25 có sẵn ở `forge/stage1_intake/search_specs.py`, nhưng là CLI rời nhận free-form query; chưa được orchestration bởi identity resolution hoặc ghi evidence vào manifest.
- Có drift cần xử lý: `forge/stage2_spec/cs2_adapters.py` đã đăng ký `pistol/glock-18`, nhưng `cs2_manifest.validate_manifest()` vẫn chỉ cho state `proceed` khi family là `knife`.

## Quyết định sản phẩm đề xuất

Tên do người dùng nhập là **declared identity**, không phải identity đã xác thực. Ảnh là nguồn sự thật cho hình học và finish quan sát được. External knowledge chỉ được dùng sau khi identity đã đủ tin cậy.

### Luồng đề xuất

1. Validate hai ảnh và gán stable view roles: `front` và `back`; kiểm tra duplicate, coverage và mâu thuẫn view.
2. Từ ảnh, tạo `observedIdentity` gồm family, subtype, item/skin candidate, confidence và evidence refs.
3. So sánh `declaredIdentity` với `observedIdentity`.
4. Chỉ khi kết quả phù hợp hoặc được người dùng xác nhận mới chọn family adapter và BM25-search specs.
5. Tự tạo query BM25 từ family, subtype, item và skin đã resolve; lưu query, match IDs, source/provenance và confidence vào manifest.
6. Tạo brief/prompt nội bộ đầy đủ; người dùng không cần mô tả chi tiết.

### Chính sách mismatch

| Tình huống | Hành vi |
| --- | --- |
| Tên và ảnh khớp | Tiếp tục, dùng BM25 và adapter đã resolve. |
| Sai skin nhưng đúng base item | Dùng anatomy/spec của base item; lấy finish, decal và wear từ ảnh. |
| Sai family/subtype | Không dùng spec của tên đã khai báo; trả `request-input` với một câu xác nhận ngắn. |
| Không có tên | Resolve từ ảnh; chỉ BM25 khi confidence đạt ngưỡng. |
| Không đủ tin cậy | Dựng image-first/provisional với suy luận được gắn confidence, hoặc yêu cầu xác nhận ngắn trước khi chọn adapter. |

## OpenSpec change đề xuất

Tạo change mới: `minimal-image-intake-and-identity-arbitration`. Không mở rộng hoặc sửa lẫn vào change CS2 cũ vì đây là UX + identity boundary mới, còn change hiện tại vẫn có calibration task chưa hoàn tất.

### Requirements cần có

- Minimal input contract: `frontImage`, `backImage`, `declaredItemName?`.
- Manifest schema tách `declaredIdentity`, `observedIdentity`, `resolvedIdentity` và `identityDecision`.
- Evidence-backed arbitration với ngưỡng confidence, mismatch reason và trạng thái `proceed` / `request-input` / `fallback`.
- BM25 orchestration chỉ chạy sau identity decision; query/result/provenance được persisted.
- Family adapter selection chỉ dùng `resolvedIdentity`; không được fallback sang family không khớp.
- Đồng bộ capability support thực tế của pistol/Glock-18 với manifest validation và docs.
- Generated internal brief ghi rõ observed vs inferred details, hidden-region confidence, material/finish evidence, component tree và review requirements.

### Acceptance scenarios

1. Hai ảnh + tên Glock-18 khớp: manifest resolve Glock-18, BM25 trả pistol/Glock specs, chọn pistol adapter.
2. Hai ảnh Glock-18 nhưng tên M9: không query/không chọn knife adapter; trả short mismatch confirmation.
3. Hai ảnh đúng base Glock-18 nhưng skin name sai: giữ Glock anatomy, finish theo ảnh và đánh dấu name mismatch.
4. Hai ảnh không có tên: resolve candidate từ visual classification, chỉ BM25 khi qua confidence threshold.
5. Hai view trùng hoặc coverage không đủ: request-input với machine-readable reason.
6. Mọi decision đều lưu evidence, confidence và provenance để review/audit.

## Ngoài scope

- Không bắt người dùng viết prompt dài.
- Không coi metadata/network lookup là required dependency.
- Không tự nhận hidden-side geometry hay texture là observed evidence.
- Không thêm generic fallback khiến item sai family được dựng theo adapter khác.

title: v1.4.1: undocumented --map-stripped-render gate makes the blockout pass unpassable from SKILL.md (3 tests failing on main)
body:
## Summary

v1.4.1 added two hard gates to `forge/stage4_review/append_review.py` but updated neither `SKILL.md` nor the test suite. Code, docs, and tests are now out of sync.

The practical effect: an agent that follows `SKILL.md` step 9 verbatim fails on `blockout`, which is the **first** review pass of every run. It cannot credit a single pass.

## 1. Three tests fail on a clean clone of `main` (9614f1a)

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s forge/tests
Ran 245 tests in 35.7s
FAILED (failures=2, errors=1)
```

```
ERROR: test_cs2_review.Cs2ReviewGateTest.test_append_review_persists_cs2_report_and_rejects_failed_report
FAIL:  test_pipeline.PipelineTest.test_append_review_gate_and_record
FAIL:  test_pipeline.PipelineTest.test_orchestrator_refuses_current_pass_without_passing_tier1
```

Two root causes, both new gates in `append_review.py main()`:

**Blockout evidence gate** (`append_review.py:282`)
```python
if args.pass_id == "blockout" and args.action == "continue" and not args.map_stripped_render:
    raise ValueError("blockout cannot be credited without --map-stripped-render (unlit, map-stripped evidence)")
```

**Ordered credit gate** (`append_review.py:277`)
```python
if args.pass_id != expected_pass and not args.force_out_of_order:
    raise ValueError(f"cannot record submitted pass {args.pass_id!r}; current unlocked pass is {expected_pass!r}. ...")
```

The three tests predate both gates and still call `append_review.py` the old way.

## 2. The docs gap (this is the part that reaches users, not just CI)

`SKILL.md:163` gives the canonical `append_review.py` invocation with ten flags. `--map-stripped-render` is not one of them. The concept is not documented anywhere in the repo:

```
$ grep -rn "map-stripped\|unlit\|maps disabled\|map-off" --include='*.md' .
(no matches)
```

`blockout` is first in the documented build order (`SKILL.md:31`), so a faithful agent run hits `ValueError` on pass 1. The failing tests are effectively the canary for a real user-facing break.

## Suggested fix

1. **Docs**: add `--map-stripped-render <shot>` to the `SKILL.md` step 9 invocation, and have step 7 instruct the agent to capture a maps-disabled render alongside the normal blockout screenshot. Mention `--force-out-of-order` for the ordered-credit rule.
2. **Tests**: update the three tests to pass `--map-stripped-render` and to credit passes in unlocked order, so the suite guards the new gates instead of tripping over them.

Happy to open a PR for either half if useful.

## Environment

- Clean clone of `main` @ `9614f1a`, no local modifications
- Python 3.12.3, macOS

body: ## What `README.md` line 3 renders ``, but that file no longer exists on `main` — so the logo 404s: https://github.com/img2threejs/img2threejs/blob/main/assets/logo.svg ## Why it went missing `chore: update readme (#31)` deleted the whole `assets/` directory **and** added `assets/` to `.gitignore`. Dropping the demo GIFs was intentional; `logo.svg` went with them by accident. ## Changes - Restore `assets/logo.svg` from the org brand source (`img2threejs-org/brand/logo-avatar.svg`, 512×512 square — matches the README's `width=112 height=112`). - Narrow the ignore rule from `assets/` to `assets/*` + `!assets/logo.svg`. The trailing `*` matters: git cannot re-include a file whose **parent directory** is excluded, so `assets/` + `!assets/logo.svg` would silently fail and the logo would need `git add -f` forever — i.e. it would quietly disappear again on the next cleanup. ## Verified - `git check-ignore` resolves `assets/logo.svg` to the negation rule; `assets/*.gif` still resolves to `assets/*` (demo GIFs stay untracked, as intended). - SVG reviewed line by line before publishing: gradients + polygons only, no scripts, no external refs, no credentials. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Vehicles need a family adapter — form predicates and coverage gates can't fire on components the spec has no vocabulary for
body: ## Summary Reconstructing a 1960s Ferrari GT berlinetta on 1.4.1, the pipeline nails every enumerated detail — wire-spoke wheels as real spoke geometry, three fender louvers, covered headlamp pods, correct wheel diameter, correct wheelbase — and gets the body form wrong in ways no gate catches. The plan view comes out as a constant-width stadium shape. Result reads as a toy of the right car rather than the car. This is not a gate-strength problem. It's that the gates have no vehicle vocabulary to evaluate against. ## The specific failure Top-down silhouette is constant width from front axle to rear axle. A real vehicle body varies width continuously along X: nose taper, front fender crown, door waist, rear hip flare, tail taper. Downstream, this makes every 3/4 view read soft, because the highlight can't travel across a form that has no cross-car curvature. Secondary, same root cause: greenhouse generated as a child object on a hard beltline ledge rather than a continuous surface into the rear deck; A-pillars as cylinders; zero tumblehome (body sides perfectly vertical). ## Why 1.4.1's gates pass it - `check_part_coverage.py` verifies specified components are built and flags collapsed meshes. Greenhouse, beltline, and pillars were never specified, so there's nothing to check coverage against. - Tier 1 geometry-integrity already detects **constant blade grinds** and **missing distal taper** — cross-section failing to vary along the long axis. That is exactly this defect. The predicate exists; there is no vehicle family for it to fire on. - `validate_sculpt_spec.py --strict-quality` measures component depth, which is domain-blind. A 40-component vehicle spec with no greenhouse or plan-taper entries is "deep" by that metric and structurally wrong by any automotive one. - The review sheet is a 3/4 view, which carries almost no information about plan-view width variation. ## Ask: a vehicle adapter, sibling to the pistol and knife adapters 1.4.1 states the Glock-18 adapter "does not reuse the knife topology." Vehicles need the same treatment — this is a second instance of an accepted pattern, not new architecture. - `vehicle` family in the intake route with its own component tree: greenhouse, DLO, beltline, tumblehome, fender crown, shoulder line, rocker undercut, wheel arch (radius + cut height), A/B/C pillar, cowl, valance, Kamm tail, plan taper - **Required plan-view section table** — width at N stations along X. Highest-value single addition; generalizes the distal-taper predicate to a second axis - **Plan-taper predicate in Tier 1** — flag constant cross-car width where the reference shows variation, exactly as constant blade grind is flagged today - **Proportion-lock pass** — wheelbase-normalized landmarks (nose, front axle, cowl, roof peak, backlight base, rear axle, tail) plus rails: greenhouse-to-total-height ratio, tire OD vs. wheelbase, track vs. overall width - **Top-down orthographic required in the review sheet** for wheeled subjects. The current 3/4-only sheet structurally cannot surface this class of defect - **Automotive material recipes** — clearcoat paint (metallic base, clearcoat 1.0, clearcoatRoughness ~0.03), chrome, glass, tire rubber, polished alloy. The candy- coat model added in 1.3 is close but tuned for CS2 finishes - **Banded studio environment** for the lighting gate. A flat white environment renders chrome as featureless grey and clearcoat as vinyl regardless of correct metalness/roughness ## Smallest useful subset Plan-view section table as a required spec field for wheeled subjects, plus a top-down in the comparison sheet. Those two catch most of the form failures alone. ## Environment img2threejs 1.4.1 (SKILL.md), HEAD f1ade81, macOS. `git describe --tags` reports `v1.3-12-gf1ade81` — 1.4.0 and 1.4.1 appear to be untagged, which makes version reporting awkward. Attaching: reference photos, side/front/top/3-4 renders, and the prompt preamble that produced this output.

title: docs: document the v1.4.1 review gates and make the suite guard them
body:
Fixes #33.

## Summary

v1.4.1 added hard gates to the review path but updated neither `SKILL.md` nor the tests. The user-facing effect is that an agent following `SKILL.md` step 9 verbatim fails on `blockout` — the **first** review pass of every run — so it cannot credit a single pass.

This PR syncs the docs and makes the test suite guard the gates instead of tripping over them. **No production code is changed.**

## The issue missed a third gate

@byosamah's report identifies two gates in `append_review.py`. There is a third, in `diagnose_render.py:273`:

```python
if args.pass_id == "blockout":
    if not args.map_stripped_render:
        result.setdefault("failures", []).append("blockout requires --map-stripped-render evidence")
        result["passed"] = False
```

This is why `test_orchestrator_refuses_current_pass_without_passing_tier1` was failing — that test never calls `append_review.py` at all. It calls `diagnose_render.py`, which records a `tier1Result` with `passed: false`, so `orchestrate_passes.py check` keeps the pass locked. Applying only the fix suggested in the issue would have left that test red.

## Docs

- **Step 7** now instructs capturing the maps-disabled `blockout` render, naming the exact maps that `strip_material_maps()` clears (`map`, `normalMap`, `roughnessMap`, `metalnessMap`, `aoMap`).
- **Step 9** documents `--map-stripped-render` and the ordered-credit rule, including `--force-out-of-order`.
- **The Tier 1 bullet** explains why `blockout` records `passed: false` without the evidence. I rewrapped it to the ~100-col convention its neighbouring bullets already use — it was the file's longest line at 336 chars and my addition would have pushed it to 539. The file's longest line is now 329, slightly shorter than before this PR.
- **`grimoire/scripts.md`** — `SKILL.md` cites this as "Full flags", and its `append_review.py` evidence-flag list was missing both new flags. Fixing `SKILL.md` while leaving the reference it points at stale would have reproduced the same bug.

I deliberately did **not** document `--map-stripped-scene` as the mechanism for producing the render. It is referenced nowhere else in the repo, nothing in the documented flow produces a scene JSON (the pipeline output is a TypeScript factory), and it rewrites its input file in place. Documenting it looked like a footgun, so step 7 states the requirement instead of prescribing an unproven workflow.

## Tests

The three failures are fixed at their real root cause rather than worked around:

- `test_pipeline` — supply `--map-stripped-render` to both `append_review.py` and `diagnose_render.py`.
- `test_cs2_review` — this test exercises the CS2 report gate, not pass ordering, so it credits out of order deliberately via `--force-out-of-order`. It now asserts on the error message with `assertRaisesRegex`; without that, the ordered-credit gate would raise first and silently mask the behaviour the test claims to check.

Plus **three new regression tests**, since nothing guarded the new gates:

| Test | Guards |
|---|---|
| `test_blockout_continue_refused_without_map_stripped_render` | `append_review.py` blockout evidence gate |
| `test_append_review_refuses_out_of_order_pass` | ordered-credit gate |
| `test_diagnose_render_fails_blockout_without_map_stripped_render` | `diagnose_render.py` blockout gate + the resulting orchestrator lock |

## Verification

```
python3 -m unittest discover -s forge/tests   ->  245 tests, 3 failing   (before)
                                              ->  248 tests, all passing (after)
python3 forge/tests/test_pipeline.py          ->  59 tests, all passing
```

Each new test was mutation-verified: disabling any one gate in the source fails exactly its own test, and only that test.

Checked against `CONTRIBUTING.md` — no emojis, stdlib only, both documented test commands pass, no production code touched. Verified on Python 3.12; the CI in #37 targets 3.10 and nothing here is version-sensitive.

## Note on ownership

@kokorolx is assigned to #33 and said this was planned for the next release. This was already written when I noticed — very happy to close it if you'd rather land your own, and the third-gate finding above stands either way.

title: fix: degenerate silhouette evidence no longer scores as a perfect match
body:
Fixes bugs 2 and 8 of #18.

## Two unrelated objects currently pass as an exact silhouette match

200×200 frames, 30×30 subjects at opposite corners, **zero shared pixels**, run against untouched `main`:

```
true silhouette overlap : ZERO
reported silhouetteIoU  : 1.0
passed                  : True
failures                : []
warning surfaced        : none
```

`build_foreground_mask` falls back to "all opaque pixels" when keyed coverage drops below 3.5%, inverting a small subject into a full frame. It *does* warn about this — and both mask consumers discarded the warning:

```python
# diagnose_render.load_mask
mask, _diag, _warn = build_foreground_mask(width, height, pixels)
```

`divine_eye.evaluate` inherited the same blindness through `load_mask`. Notably `diagnose_render_multi_angle.py:52` already handles this correctly, so the repo contained both the right and the wrong pattern.

Separately, `silhouette_iou` and `edge_overlap` both returned `1.0` on an empty union. Two blank frames therefore also scored a perfect match, and `edge_overlap` contributed a free 1.0-weighted term to the fidelity ensemble.

The common thread: **absence of evidence was being scored as agreement.**

## Changes

**`diagnose_render.py`**
- `load_mask` returns `(mask, warnings)` rather than dropping them. This is a signature change; both in-repo callers are updated.
- New `mask_is_inverted()` helper, matching the convention already used in `diagnose_render_multi_angle.py`.
- `run_tier1` gates on it *before* reading IoU, fails with an explicit unusable-evidence reason, and surfaces `maskWarnings` in its result.
- Empty union → `0.0`.

**`divine_eye.py`**
- `evaluate` raises the same condition as a hard gate and reports `maskWarnings`.
- `edge_overlap` empty union → `0.0`.

## On the objectness rescue path

I initially added a `not mask_inverted` guard to the reconstruction-mode rescue. Mutation testing showed removing it changed nothing, so I dug in: the rescue requires `all("silhouette IoU" in f for f in hard_failures)`, and the inversion failure message is not an IoU failure, so the rescue is already unreachable in this state (objectness is `0.0` there regardless).

It was dead code and the test I had written to justify it proved nothing, so I removed both and left a comment recording the invariant and naming the test that backstops it if the message is ever reworded. Flagging it here because it is the kind of thing that looks like a deliberate safety guard in review when it is actually unreachable.

## Tests

7 regression tests across `test_divine_eye.py` and `test_pipeline.py`, covering the unit level (`silhouette_iou`, `edge_overlap`, `mask_is_inverted`), the `evaluate` level (disjoint subjects; identical subjects at different positions, where every non-silhouette signal agrees and only this gate separates it from a real match), and the Tier-1 CLI level.

Every guard was mutation-verified — reverting any one of the five individually fails exactly its own test:

```
silhouette_iou empty -> 1.0            CAUGHT
edge_overlap empty -> 1.0              CAUGHT
tier1 inversion gate removed           CAUGHT
divine_eye inversion gate removed      CAUGHT
same-shape case vs inversion gate      CAUGHT
```

## Verification

```
245 -> 252 tests, zero new failures
```

The 3 failures on this branch are pre-existing on `main` and are exactly the ones from #33. **This PR should land after the #33 fix**, after which the combined suite is **255 tests, all passing** (verified locally). The two touch adjacent lines in `test_pipeline.py`, so whichever merges second needs a one-line conflict resolution — happy to rebase on request.

## Credit

Bugs 2 and 8 come from @cktang88's audit in #18, which is unusually thorough. I re-verified both independently against current `main` with my own repro scripts before writing anything, and can confirm:

- **Bug 1 (scale-gate key mismatch) is already fixed** on `main` — the audit was filed against `7b1c62c`.
- **Bugs 3, 4 and 5 are still live.** Bug 4 in particular reproduces exactly as described: a lathe primitive with no profile data passes plain validation, and the generator exits 0 emitting the hardcoded default hourglass with no marker — four lines below a docstring promising *"Never silently substitute a box... with no signal that anything was wrong."*

@cktang88 offered to send PRs for these. I've only taken 2 and 8 and am glad to leave the rest, or to help with them if that's useful.

title: fix: decode JPEG in-process so reference images work off macOS
body:
## img2threejs cannot read a JPEG reference on Linux or Windows

The pipeline's input is a reference image. JPEG — the most common format a reference photo arrives in — only works on macOS.

Every `load_image()` falls back to the macOS `sips` binary for non-PNG input, and `shutil.which("sips")` returns `None` everywhere else:

```
ValueError: could not decode reference.jpg as PNG and macOS sips is unavailable: not a PNG file
```

Verified by monkeypatching `shutil.which` to `None` — the same failure occurs in **all five** copies of this fallback: `extract_pbr_evidence.py`, `extract_landmarks.py`, `delight_albedo.py`, `build_detail_inventory.py`, `make_comparison_sheet.py`.

The CI added in #37 runs on `ubuntu-latest`, so any test touching a JPEG would fail there today.

## Approach

Pillow is not an option — `CONTRIBUTING.md` requires pure stdlib, no pip. So this adds `forge/_shared/jpeg.py`, a baseline JPEG decoder written against the same constraint.

Scope is deliberately narrow and says so in its own docstring:

- baseline (SOF0) and extended sequential (SOF1) DCT, 8-bit
- grayscale and YCbCr, any sampling factors, restart intervals
- progressive, arithmetic, 12-bit and CMYK raise `UnsupportedJpeg` so callers fall back rather than silently mis-decode

Each `load_image()` tries the decoder before `sips`. **`sips` stays as the fallback** for formats not decoded here (HEIC, TIFF) — no existing behaviour is removed, and macOS users see no change.

## Accuracy

Measured against the **original pre-JPEG source**, not against another decoder — comparing two decoders only tells you they disagree, not which is right:

| fixture | this decoder vs original | libjpeg/sips vs original |
|---|---|---|
| gradient | max 3, mean 0.526 | max 4, mean 0.544 |
| odd_size (37×23) | max 4, mean 0.552 | max 5, mean 0.608 |
| two_blocks | max 1, mean 0.167 | max 1, mean 0.333 |

Decoder-vs-decoder differences of a few units are expected and permitted — ISO/IEC 10918 leaves IDCT precision implementation-defined. This float IDCT lands marginally closer to the source than libjpeg's integer path on every fixture.

Chroma is upsampled with a triangular filter rather than nearest-neighbour replication. That matters: with replication, a sharp colour edge was off by **33/255** against the reference; with the filter it is **2/255**.

## Tests

7 tests, with the JPEG fixture **embedded as base64** so they run identically on Linux CI where `sips` does not exist.

`JpegPortabilityTest` is the one that matters: it patches `shutil.which` to `None` and asserts all five `load_image()` entry points read a JPEG. That test fails on `main`.

Mutation-verified — each of these fails exactly its own test:

```
chroma upsampling scale broken     CAUGHT
JPEG wiring removed                CAUGHT
progressive guard removed          CAUGHT
```

One honest gap: the half-pixel chroma siting offset is spec conformance (it is what libjpeg's fancy upsampling does), but none of my fixtures discriminate it — removing it changes no measured output. I kept it as the standard-conformant behaviour rather than claim test coverage I do not have.

## Verification

```
245 -> 252 tests
```

The 3 failures on this branch are pre-existing on `main` (#33, fixed by #39) and untouched here. This PR is independent of #39 and #40 and can merge in any order.

## Deliberately not included

`read_png()` and `load_image()` are duplicated **verbatim across all five modules** — roughly 400 lines of copy-paste, which is why this bug had to be fixed in five places. Consolidating them into `_shared/` is the obvious follow-up, but it is a refactor of core I/O and should not ride along inside a bug fix. Happy to open it separately if you want it.
