title: strict-quality is unsatisfiable for any fabric material with a woven cue (blocks codegen)
body:
**Version:** 2.0.0 (`6e60b5e`) · **Profile:** `generic`, no plugins installed · **Subject:** a wool/leather/knit garment

## Summary

`--strict-quality` cannot be satisfied by any `fabric` material that carries a woven cue, and since `generate_threejs_factory.py` is fail-closed on strict, **no factory can be emitted for such a material at all**.

## The contradiction

`forge/_shared/material_physics.py` enforces two rules that cannot both hold:

- **`:150-158`** — `sheen > 0` with no `sheenColor` is a **hard error**: *"three's default sheenColor is #000000 and the sheen term is a multiply by that colour, so this contributes exactly zero. Declare sheenColor."*
- **`:69-72` + `:184-195`** — `("sheen", "sheenColor")` is listed in `COLLAPSED_DEGREES_OF_FREEDOM`, so declaring **both** raises `quality: ... these are not independent evidence`.
- **`:163-170`** — whenever sheen is active, `sheenEnergyComp` raises a second `quality:` warning advising base-colour compensation. It fires unconditionally, and there is no field in which to record that the compensation *was* applied — so it fires even when the authored base is already pre-brightened by exactly the factor the message asks for.

`validate_sculpt_spec.py --strict-quality` promotes every `quality:` warning to an error, and `generate_threejs_factory.py:4072-4076` refuses to write a factory when strict fails.

## Reproduction

Author one `fabric` material three ways and run `validate_sculpt_spec.py <spec> --strict-quality`:

| configuration | exit | result |
|---|---|---|
| `sheen: 0.7` + `sheenColor: "#f2ece2"` — the only combination that renders a woven cue | `1` | 4 strict errors |
| `sheen: 0.7`, no `sheenColor` | `1` | hard error, "contributes exactly zero" |
| no sheen at all | **`0`** | passes — and has no woven cue |

Only the third passes, and the repo's own guidance makes it the wrong answer: `grimoire/build/threejs_skin_and_cloth_materials.md:196-206` states sheen *"is the whole of the woven cue available to a code-only pipeline"*, and the material registry notes that a `fabric` family shipping no sheen tint has no woven cue at all.

## Why `--allow-nonstrict` is not a workaround

`generate_threejs_factory.py:4059-4084` labels it test-only, prints `WARNING: generating a non-production test-fixture factory`, and refuses to combine it with `--pass-id` — which the locked-pass workflow requires.

## Suggested fix

Either exempt these two advisories from strict promotion, or add a field (e.g. `sheenEnergyCompensated: true`) that silences the darkening advisory once the author has compensated. Note that the `ior`/`reflectivity` pair in the same tuple *is* a genuine either-or — `reflectivity` is a derived accessor over `ior`, so authoring one is correct. `sheen`/`sheenColor` is not analogous: three.js requires both for the term to evaluate to anything.

title: extract_pbr_evidence: interior crops can be masked away entirely, and confidence does not drop
body:
**Version:** 2.0.0 (`6e60b5e`)

## Summary

On an **interior material crop** — a crop that is 100% material, with no background in it — `build_foreground_mask` can discard nearly all of the material, and the reported confidence does not fall. In my case it *rose*, and the run reported `"verdict": "pass"` with `0.854` confidence while the extracted albedo map was almost entirely black.

## Mechanism

`forge/stage1_intake/extract_pbr_evidence.py:243-280`. For an opaque image the mask is:

```
alpha > 16 and (distance_from_corner_background > threshold
                or (saturation > 0.16 and luma < 0.94))
```

That test assumes a subject sitting on a background. On an interior crop **the corner is the material**, so `distance` is ~0 for every pixel of it. A bright, unsaturated material then also fails the second clause.

My crop was cream leather at saturation **0.066**, comfortably under the 0.16 threshold, so essentially the whole crop failed both clauses. What survived was the shadowed folds and a sliver of adjacent navy.

The `coverage < 0.035` rescue at `:265-268` did not fire, because that surviving residue exceeded the floor.

## Measured

94x146 crop of cream leather from a garment photograph:

| | crop mean RGB | extracted albedo mean RGB | reported confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain opaque crop | (149.7, 145.6, 136.8) | **(5.0, 6.7, 16.6)** | **0.854 "pass"** |
| same crop, transparent border | (149.7, 145.6, 136.8) | (147.9, 143.7, 135.3) | 0.860 "pass" |

Extracted palette went from `#030510, #010106, #36322C, ...` to `#F4EFDF, #918C85, #56514D` — i.e. from near-black to the actual cream. A rib-knit crop lost its white and grey stripes the same way; those returned as `#6D6C6A` after the fix.

**The confidence score is the part that worries me most.** It scores the internal consistency of whatever survived the mask, not whether the mask kept the right pixels — so a near-total masking failure reads as slightly *better* evidence than a correct extraction.

## Workaround

Pad the crop with a transparent border so `transparentPixelFraction > 0.03`. That selects the `alpha > 24` branch at `:255-257`, which is the correct mask for a crop of pure material.

## Suggested fix

Either an explicit `--interior-crop` flag that skips the corner-background test, or a warning when the sampled `backgroundColor` lands within `threshold` of the crop's own mean — that coincidence is the signature of the corner test being applied to an image with no background in it.

title: analyze_texture assigns metal finish classes to fabric and silently rewrites authored roughness
body:
**Version:** 2.0.0 (`6e60b5e`) · **Profile:** `generic`, no domain plugins installed

## Summary

Run against verified interior crops of a wool/leather/knit garment with `--spec ... --in-place`, `analyze_texture.py` assigned every fabric a metal finish class and silently rewrote the authored roughness scalars to match.

| material | actual finish | assigned `finishClass` | roughness before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| wool melton | woven matte | **`painted-metal`** | 0.92 → 0.50 |
| leather | pebbled dielectric | **`brushed-steel`** | 0.50 → 0.35 |
| rib knit | knit matte | **`candy-coat`** | 0.85 → **0.18** |

A rib knit at roughness 0.18 renders as polished plastic.

## What I think is happening

The finish vocabulary looks weapon-skin oriented (`painted-metal`, `brushed-steel`, `candy-coat`). With no domain plugin installed there is no fabric class available, so each crop is forced into the nearest class rather than the classification being refused. No warning is emitted, and the spec is patched in place.

The crops themselves were verified first — I had already checked each one visually to confirm it was on the part I thought it was, and the corresponding `extract_pbr_evidence` runs returned 0.80–0.86 confidence on the same pixels.

## Suggested fix

Two things, either of which would have caught this:

1. **Refuse to classify** when no finish class is within some confidence bound, rather than returning the nearest match. "I do not have a class for this" is a useful answer.
2. **Never silently overwrite an authored roughness scalar.** The repo's own rule (`grimoire/build/threejs_skin_and_cloth_materials.md:115-116`) is that roughness is *reported, never gated*, because screen-space `geometryRoughness` is added at shade time — so an authored value being replaced by an inferred one is a meaningful loss, and it happens with no record in the spec that it occurred.

Related: #135, #136 — all three surfaced in the same run, and all three share a root cause in the intake and material tooling assuming a rigid, saturated object photographed against a background.

title: Extract the character domain into plugin-character: the base now names no domain
body:
Extracts the character domain from this repo into `plugin-character`, completing the v2.0 plugin
split: **`forge/_shared/domains/` now ships no domain module at all.**

Paired with img2threejs/plugin-character#2. OpenSpec change:
`extract-character-sculpt-into-the-plugin` (two adversarial reviews, plus an independent partition
review that rebutted four of its seven questions as malformed).

## The rule this is measured by

> The character build emits the same Three.js output for the same input across the move.

Not sampled — **proved by md5 over the full emitted TypeScript**, through the real installed plugin
and this base, with nothing stubbed:

```
$ ~/.img2/plugins/character/tools/emit_spec_augmentation.py --anatomy anatomy.json --out spec-augmentation.json
{"kind":"spec-augmentation-v1","components":61,"bones":49,"materials":9}

$ forge/stage2_spec/new_sculpt_spec.py "Oracle Figure" --augmentation spec-augmentation.json --domain character --out oracle.json
$ generate(oracle.json, "blockout")

produced md5: 98ac2045dcc9d802cc369e8b4d4d20a4
frozen   md5: 98ac2045dcc9d802cc369e8b4d4d20a4   <- forge/tests/fixtures/oracle-character/blockout.ts
BYTE-IDENTICAL
```

## Breaking

| | |
|---|---|
| `--profile animated-character` | **withdrawn** → `--profile character`. One id now, always carrying the nine Stage R rig steps. A second profile that omitted them is how animation shipped broken in 1.5.1 |
| `--profile character` | now requires plugin-character ≥ 0.3.0 installed |
| `new_sculpt_spec.py --character` / `--accessories` | **removed and refused**, not ignored |
| `new_pre_spec_assessment.py --character` | removed |
| `character-v1.5` | no longer a pipeline track |
| `validate_character_track` | removed with the template it gated |
| `rig_is_bone_track` | routes on `rig.bones` alone |

A withdrawn profile now gets a message that answers the question the user actually has:

```
state error: profile 'animated-character' has been withdrawn; it was replaced by 'character'.
             one id now carries the rig steps; a static build skips a rig step with a recorded
             reason. Re-init with --profile character, or edit "profile" in an in-flight state
             file. Available: generic.
```

The old message said only *"no installed provider serves profile 'animated-character'; available:
…"* — from which "your plugin is missing" and "this profile no longer exists" are
indistinguishable — and its advice, *install the plugin that provides it*, cannot succeed: nobody
provides it, so obeying it reproduces the message.

## Three decisions worth reviewing rather than skimming

**1. `character` and `hybrid` stay in `VALID_KINDS` while `character-v1.5` leaves `TRACK_BY_KIND`.**
A KIND is what the classifier saw; a TRACK is what this repo can build from it. Dropping the kind
would make a correct, confident classification come back as `malformed-classification` — "a
character" and "corrupt input" would read identically, a regression in a gate whose entire value is
explaining its refusal. A `character` classification now fails closed naming `--domain character`,
rather than resolving to `request-input` with an **empty** conflicts list (which rendered as the
literal string `pipeline routing requires input: ` and nothing after it).

**2. `rig_is_bone_track` drops its domain allow-list — a real behaviour change, not a cleanup.**
A spec carrying `rig.bones` with `primaryDomain: "object"` went from emitting **nothing** to
emitting a full skeleton. `rig` is not in `BASE_OWNED`, so any domain may now author bones; a
domain-name allow-list here would have meant the base deciding which domains are allowed to have
skeletons. Owned by name in `test_rig_hierarchy_emission.py` rather than hidden behind "no fixture
regresses".

**3. `state.py` drops `choices=` on `--profile`.** One bad profile gave two different answers —
`init` printed argparse's list, `resume` went through the registry and explained itself.

## Verification

- `IMG2_HOME=$(mktemp -d) pytest forge/tests` → **1391 passed, 66 skipped, 0 failed, 0 errors**
- `COLLECTED_FLOOR` **set** to the measured **1457**, from 1192 against 1458 — 266 of slack, enough
  to absorb a quarter of the suite going dark. That slack is how a previous, withdrawn attempt lost
  100 tests with nothing going red. Arithmetic is written into `test_suite_integrity.py`.
- `img2 doctor` → `ok (4 plugins, 1 warning)`; the warning is the expected multi-capability notice.

**Every test that broke got a disposition, never a deletion to make the suite green.** Five
`test_pipeline.py` tests that drove `--character` moved to the plugin's authoring oracle with their
subject; three modules that built a humanoid fixture by shelling out to `--character` now read the
frozen oracle spec (same bytes, no subprocess); the registry tests that leaned on an in-repo
`character` are re-expressed against two *installed* fixture plugins, which is the stronger form of
the same claim.

## Two gates from the `openspec-apply-audit` skill

```
g5_surviving_readers.py forge/ --dest character --dest accessories  ->  0 findings
g3_moved_not_copied.py  (19 symbols)                                ->  19 MOVED, 0 COPIED/VANISHED
```

G5 is the withdrawn attempt's signature defect: it deleted `--character` and left `args.character`,
raising `AttributeError` on **every** profile including generic. A string-literal AST sweep cannot
see it, because `args.character` contains no string constant.

## New: `forge/tests/test_documentation_agreement.py`

Two classes of doc rot, checked by the suite rather than by a command someone remembers:
dead paths in live guidance (**Python docstrings included** — `extract_landmarks.py:6` named a page
that moved while the module stayed), and a withdrawn identifier surviving in prose. The second is
the half a path-scoped check cannot do: `--profile animated-character` is not a path, which is how
seven documents kept teaching the withdrawn profile while the one mechanical doc gate passed green.

## What two rounds of review changed, after the capture above

Recorded because a PR that only lists what passed is the shape the withdrawn attempt had.

**A cleanup review** found `SECTION_AUTHORITY`'s plugin half checked only from the *other* repo, by
a test that skips when it cannot see this one. It is now also checked from here, scoped to what this
repo can actually verify — the first version of that test asserted every non-base-owned section in
the frozen spec needs a ruling, which was wrong on a false premise: `BASE_OWNED` is a deny-list of
what a plugin may not *write*, not a list of what the base does not author. The frozen spec carries
24 sections the base authors itself.

**A correctness review** found one Critical and three Important. Two are this repo's:

- **The routing conflict's remedy could not succeed.** The message named `--domain character` plus a
  spec-augmentation artifact; supplying both reproduced the message, because the routing check ran
  before the block that reads those flags. The precise failure the withdrawal table was written to
  avoid, repeated one file over. **The first fix was worse than none** — it let the run through with
  the record still `request-input`, which exited 0 here and then failed `strict-validation` with
  "pipelineRouting must be resolved before validation". So `resolve_pipeline_routing` now takes
  `provider_domain` and owns the verdict, rather than having it patched by a caller writing a field
  whose invariants live in that module. A provider-resolved record carries `track: null` and names
  its provider; it answers exactly one conflict, and a hybrid, an unknown, a shaky classification or
  a provider claiming a different kind all still fail closed.
- **`SKILL.md:81` was left truncated** by an earlier edit — an orphan clause with no verb, and the
  claim "on `character` the Stage R gates are absent", which contradicted the clause three lines
  above it. `test_documentation_agreement` could not catch it: no dead path, and the withdrawn
  identifier had been edited out of the sentence.

The Critical was the plugin's, and it reaches back here: `validate_character_track` was deleted under
a disposition **I wrote** asserting the check had moved to the producer. It had not — the producer
exited 0 with no anatomy at all. The gate briefly existed in neither repo.
`forge/tests/test_pipeline.py` now records that, rather than quietly correcting it: a disposition is
a claim about another repo, and this suite cannot verify one.

## Known limitation, stated rather than worked around

The **rig half** of the end-to-end acceptance is blocked, and the blocker is pre-existing:
`runtime/scripts/export_mesh_buffers.mjs` is invoked by two of the nine rig steps and does not
exist in this repo — it shipped that way in plugin-character v0.2.0. This change does not make the
rig track runnable end to end, and it did not break it either. Full capture:
`openspec/changes/extract-character-sculpt-into-the-plugin/review/acceptance.md`.

title: [Bug]: search-specs CLI crashes with UnicodeEncodeError on non-UTF-8 consoles
body:
## What happened?

`forge/stage1_intake/search_specs.py` prints query text and result snippets with `ensure_ascii=False` straight to `print()`. When stdout is not UTF-8 (Windows console with a non-UTF-8 code page, or any host with `PYTHONIOENCODING` set to a legacy codec), any non-ASCII query or snippet crashes the CLI with `UnicodeEncodeError` instead of returning results. I expected the CLI to emit UTF-8 output and exit 0 regardless of the console encoding, since every source file and cache in this pipeline is UTF-8.

## Reproduction steps

1. From the skill root, force a non-UTF-8 stdout encoding (portable on any OS):

   PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii python3 forge/stage1_intake/search_specs.py --collection cs2 rough --json

   Any query whose snippets contain non-ASCII text (for example the Vietnamese fixture terms) triggers it.
2. Observe a traceback ending in `UnicodeEncodeError` and exit code 1, instead of the JSON payload.

The repo's own suite covers this path: `test_human_output_is_nonempty_and_stable_on_cache_hits` and `test_untruncated_snippet_has_no_ellipses` in `forge/tests/test_search_specs.py` search fixture corpora containing Vietnamese terms and an ellipsis snippet. Both pass on UTF-8 hosts and fail on Windows default consoles.

## Reference image or input characteristics

Not image-related. Input: any search query plus an indexed corpus containing non-ASCII text (Vietnamese terms, ellipsis U+2026). Output: the JSON or human-readable result listing passed through `print()` with `ensure_ascii=False`.

## Relevant output and evidence

Child-process stderr on a cp1252 Windows console:

    File "forge/stage1_intake/search_specs.py", line 143, in _print_human
        print(f"Query: {payload['query']}")
    UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters: character maps to <undefined>

The JSON path fails identically in `_print_json` (`json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)` written to a cp1252 stream). The same print pattern exists across other forge CLIs, but this issue is scoped to `search_specs.py`; the rest can follow the same remedy once agreed.

## Environment

- img2threejs version or commit: upstream/main 6e60b5e
- Python version: 3.14.3 (Windows; repo toolchain is python3, invoked here via the py launcher)
- Host agent: OpenCode
- Operating system: Windows 11 (cp1252 console); portable repro via PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii on any OS

title: fix(materials): treat sheen+sheenColor co-declaration as informational, add sheenEnergyCompensated gate
body:
## Summary

Refs #135. Co-declaring `sheen` and `sheenColor` in a material spec currently trips the collapsed-degrees-of-freedom gate as a `quality:` warning, so a correctly authored fabric (both fields, per the repo's own docs) fails `--strict-quality`. That contradicts the engine: three.js requires **both** fields for the sheen term to evaluate at all — the default `sheenColor` is black and the term is a multiply, so `sheen` alone contributes nothing (`WebGLMaterials.js:408`, `ShaderLib/meshphysical.glsl.js:205`).

This PR separates the two cases the gate was conflating:
- `sheen` × `sheenColor` — folded into one uniform, but **co-declaration is required authorship**, reported as an informational note, never a `quality:` gate.
- `ior` ↔ `reflectivity` — a genuine either-or (reflectivity is a derived accessor over ior), and setting both stays an error.

It also closes the loop the darkening advisory left open: once an author pre-brightens the base by `1/(1−darkening)` to offset sheen energy absorption, there was no way to record that, so `--strict-quality` blocked valid compensated materials forever. A `sheenEnergyCompensated: true` material field now silences the advisory; the flag is author metadata only and the generator ignores it.

## Changes

- `forge/_shared/material_physics.py`
  - Removed `(sheen, sheenColor, ...)` from `COLLAPSED_DEGREES_OF_FREEDOM`; co-declaration now emits an informational note (no `quality:` prefix, never promoted by `--strict-quality`).
  - The collapsed-pair loop now emits errors only — every remaining pair in the tuple is either-or by construction.
  - The sheen darkening advisory gains an escape hatch: suppressed only by `sheenEnergyCompensated is True` (a falsy or non-bool value does not silence it).
  - Docstring documents which warnings `--strict-quality` promotes.
- `forge/tests/test_material_physics.py` — 5 new regression tests (18 total in the file), including the strict-pass case from the issue, the falsy-flag guard, and the unaffected no-sheen fabric warning.
- `docs/materials/material-reference.json` — updated the two notes to document co-declaration as correct authorship and the compensation flag.
- `grimoire/build/threejs_skin_and_cloth_materials.md` — S-2 and section 4 rewritten to split the pairs; darkening section documents the flag; checklist updated.

## Validation

- [x] `python3 forge/tests/test_pipeline.py` — 57/57 OK (168s)
- [x] `forge/tests/test_material_physics.py` — 18/18 OK, including `test_sheen_and_sheen_color_together_are_informational_not_quality` and `test_compensated_fabric_sheen_passes_strict`, which fail without the fix
- [ ] Render or comparison-sheet review, if applicable — not applicable; validator/doc change only, no generated output changes

## Contributor checklist

- [x] This PR keeps the code-only procedural reconstruction contract; it does not silently download meshes or art packs.
- [x] Existing object specs remain valid — co-declared specs that previously failed `--strict-quality` now pass; no spec that passed before fails now.

- [x] I updated documentation and roadmap status where applicable.

title: Add strict-quality gate for dimensions/transform.scale mismatch
body:
## Summary
- Fixes #108: a component authored with real `dimensions` but left at a scaffolded `transform.scale: [1,1,1]` silently renders at its primitive's unit size instead of its authored size, since `generate_threejs_factory.py` reads `transform.scale` whenever the key is present at all and never falls back to `dimensions` once it does. This is large enough to bury smaller attached parts entirely (e.g. a character's arms and hat vanishing inside an oversized torso/head), which is how it was found.
- Adds `validate_dimension_scale_consistency()` to `forge/stage2_spec/validate_sculpt_spec.py`, flagged under `--strict-quality`, mirroring the generator's own endpoint-gating logic so it only fires on components actually sized this way (attachment-derived primitives like cylinders/cones/capsules are correctly exempted, since those are sized from `attachment.baseRadius`/`length` instead).
- The new gate also caught the exact same latent defect in this repo's own `forge/tests/fixtures/reference_target_conformance_spec.json` (11 components with real dimensions and identity scale) — fixed the fixture's scale values and re-recorded `reference_target_oracle.ts` accordingly, per that test file's own stated policy for legitimate drift.

title: fix(orchestrate): material-pass honours the textureless declaration
body:
## What changes

`material-pass` now honours the `textureless` declaration.

The quality-first material bar is implemented in two places. `validate_sculpt_spec.py` exempts a material that declares, with evidence, that its subject carries no texture detail; its docstring explains why (a flat-shaded subject whose identity is silhouette, proportion and flat colour boundaries, for which fabricating texture resolution and frequency bands "put numbers in the spec that describe nothing"). The copy in `orchestrate_passes.py::material_pass_gaps` did not apply that exemption.

Net effect before this change: a spec whose materials are declared textureless passes `--strict-quality`, but `generate_threejs_factory.py --pass-id material-pass` refuses with `needs spec refinement: ... textureResolution must be >= 1024 ... missing surface frequency bands ... needs usable referencePbr` for every material. Because `passGateMode` is `locked-sequential`, `surface-pass`, `lighting-pass`, `interaction-pass` and `optimization-pass` are all unreachable behind it.

The fix applies the same exemption at the pass gate, through the same `is_textureless` predicate imported from `validate_sculpt_spec`, so the two bars cannot drift apart again. The skip is as guarded here as in the validator: the declaration is hard-validated there, cannot be taken without evidence, and cannot coexist with any texture-authoring field (`validate_textureless`).

Related to #120 (same shape: an acceptance bar unreachable for a legitimate material class), but a different mechanism.

## How it was found

Reconstructing a flat vector brand mark (three concentric torus rings, four tick marks, an arrow). All four materials are flat fills or two-stop analytic ramps, declared `textureless` per the validator's contract. `--strict-quality` passed with zero warnings; `material-pass` was refused with the message above. Tracing the message to `quality_first_material_gaps` showed the loop skips `qualityTier == "utility"` but never consults `is_textureless`, while the validator's loop (around line 2438) does, with a comment stating the intent.

## Verification

- `python -m unittest discover -s forge/tests` on the final tree: `Ran 1418 tests ... OK (skipped=63)`. (Local run on Python 3.12; nothing in the change is version-specific beyond 3.10.)
- New tests in `forge/tests/test_textureless_material.py`, class `TheMaterialPassGateHonoursTheDeclaration`:
  - a declared-textureless material yields no `material_pass_gaps` under `qualityPriority: reference-fidelity`;
  - control: the same material without the declaration still hits the texture-channel bar (`textureResolution must be >= 1024`).
  - Verified in both run modes, since the file has a `__main__` guard: `python test_textureless_material.py` (direct) and `unittest discover` both report 14 tests OK and both list the new class.
- End to end on the reconstruction that surfaced it: with the fix, `material-pass` generated, and the remaining four passes completed through `orchestrate_passes.py sync` to `currentPass: complete`. Render hash unchanged across those passes, as expected for a textureless subject.

## Notes for review

- No behaviour change for any material that does not declare `textureless`: the control test pins that.
- `orchestrate_passes.py` gains a `sys.path` entry for `stage2_spec`, mirroring how `generate_threejs_factory.py` already imports from `validate_sculpt_spec`.
- CHANGELOG: `### Fixed` entry under `[Unreleased]`.

title: Ship the npx installer (bin/cli.mjs) so users can install the img2threejs skill with one command
body:
## Why

The `img2threejs` skill currently requires a manual `git clone` into one of several hard-coded skills directories (`~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.codex/skills/`, `~/.config/opencode/skills/`). For users on more than one agent host, the only documented way to keep them aligned is a manual symlink dance — and the README itself warns that following the install step literally creates the divergent layout the next step warns against.

A working branch (`origin/feat/npx-skill-installer`, commits `bb2314f` + `675306a`) already implements the full fix — `bin/cli.mjs` (917 lines, zero deps, Node built-ins only), a root `package.json` publishing the `img2threejs` CLI to npm, a CI workflow `npm-publish.yml` that publishes from release tags, and 600 lines of tests in `forge/tests/test_skill_installer.py`. The branch has been open since 2026-08-21 and never merged.

- PR #61 was closed as superseded by the img2 harness approach (plugin management — different scope)
- PR #99 (the original re-pick of the branch) was closed 2026-09-02 without merge
- The harness approach (`img2threejs/img2`) solved plugins, not the skill itself; the README still says `git clone`

This change re-picks up the branch, rebases it onto current `main` (two months of drift), runs the 600-line test suite, end-to-end installs on this VPS, and ships it via npm.

## What Changes

- **Rebase `origin/feat/npx-skill-installer` onto current `main`** — resolve conflicts in `README.md` / `CHANGELOG.md` / `SKILL.md` / `ROADMAP.md`; preserve `bb2314f` + `675306a` intact
- **Land `bin/cli.mjs`** — interactive + flag-driven installer: detects Claude Code / Codex CLI / OpenCode hosts, links every selected host to one canonical checkout at `~/.img2threejs/repo`, `install` / `update` / `uninstall`
- **Land root `package.json`** — publishes `img2threejs` CLI to npm (claim `@img2threejs` scope — currently unclaimed, 0 packages)
- **Land `.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml`** — fires on `v*` tags, runs tests before publish, `--provenance` only in publish job
- **Fix version-drift bug** in `beta-release.yml` (currently touches `SKILL.md` alone — rewrite all four files in one commit)
- **Add `forge/tests/test_skill_installer.py`** — 600 lines of tests (shebang, no `prepare` lifecycle, bare-`npx` forbidden, EOF defaults to no)
- **End-to-end verify on VPS** — install / update / uninstall / re-install idempotency

## Status of working branch

```
675306a ci: publish the installer to npm from a release tag
bb2314f feat: install the skill with npx instead of a hand-run git clone
```

12 files changed, +1760 / -13. Local `main` is at `6e60b5e` (current); branch needs rebase but the changes are concentrated and additive.

## Plan

The OpenSpec change `ship-npx-installer` is scaffolded in `img2threejs-studio/openspec/changes/ship-npx-installer/` with:
- `proposal.md` — Why / What Changes / Capabilities / Impact
- `tasks.md` — 6 numbered groups, each checkbox with a verification step
- `specs/skill-installer/spec.md` — 14 ADDED Requirements covering: canonical checkout + symlink, adoption of existing clones, channel-based update, receipt-based uninstall, zero-dep constraint, shebang, EOF handling, env-var honoring, qualified-`npx` rule, CI provenance, dist-tags, version-sync, Windows-as-unverified

`openspec validate ship-npx-installer --strict` passes.

## Open questions for maintainer

1. Is the branch `feat/npx-skill-installer` still the right base, or do you want a fresh branch given the 2-month drift?
2. Claim `@img2threejs` npm scope under the `kokorolx` account (4 packages already published there) — confirm before I touch npm
3. Is there an existing `NPM_TOKEN` or do we need to provision it for the workflow?
4. First publish version — the branch ships as `1.4.4-beta.2`; current `main` is post-`v2.0.0`. Coordinate on first stable tag (likely `v2.1.0` given the recent character-split changelog)
5. Windows link creation is unverified by the original branch — accept that as a documented caveat, or block on Windows CI first?

Refs #61, #99.

title: feat: img2threejs CLI package (npx img2threejs install)
body:
Adds the `img2threejs` npm package — the install command for the img2threejs skill.

```bash
npx img2threejs install        # install into all detected agent hosts
npx img2threejs doctor         # show detected hosts + current state
npx img2threejs --version
```

This PR carries part 1 (source, tests, .gitignore). The companion PR
workflow files (`.github/workflows/cli-validate.yml` + `cli-publish.yml`)
follow once an account with `workflow` scope is available to push them,
because gh's PAT refuses workflow content otherwise.

### What's in this PR

- `package.json`: name=img2threejs, bin=bin/img2threejs.mjs, engines>=18,
  publishConfig=public. Top-level `version` field is the CLI's own semver,
  independent of the skill's `SKILL.md` version.
- `bin/img2threejs.mjs`: install/update/doctor/version subcommands. All
  subprocess calls go through `execFileSync` with argv arrays — no shell.
  Ref validation refuses `main` branches and short SHAs; only `vX.Y.Z`
  tags and 40-char SHAs pass. Resolution is delegated to
  `npx img2 add img2threejs/img2threejs --ref ...` so skill install has
  a single source of truth with the plugin install path.
- `bin/img2threejs.mjs-test.mjs`: 14 self-test assertions; no network, no
  fs writes outside TMPDIR. `npm test` exits non-zero on any failure.
- `.gitignore`: adds `node_modules/`, `package-lock.json`,
  `npm-debug.log*`, `.npmrc`.

### What's in the follow-up PR (needs workflow scope)

- `.github/workflows/cli-validate.yml`: PR-time validator. Runs
  `npm test` + `npm pack --dry-run` + bin-entry check + forbidden-hook
  guard. No secrets.
- `.github/workflows/cli-publish.yml`: tag-driven publisher reusing
  `img2threejs/ci-workflows/.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml`
  (PR #2 on ci-workflows). Pinning SHA refresh note lives in the file.

### Verification

```
$ npm test
img2threejs CLI self-test: 14 passed, 0 failed

$ npm pack --dry-run
npm notice package size: 24.5 kB
```

title: [Contribution]: priority-ordered bounded fitting for equal render budgets
body:
### What are you proposing?

A bounded new fitting primitive, motivated by downstream mesh-fidelity experiments.

### Target issue URL or number

New bounded improvement to `forge/stage4_review/fit_params.py`.

### Problem

The bounded fitter currently evaluates coordinates in one hard-coded index order. For cheap objectives that is fine. For `fit_against_divine_eye()`, each candidate can require a mesh rebuild + render + image evaluation, so a small `max_evaluations` budget may be exhausted before a caller's highest-value geometry dimensions are tested.

There is currently no deterministic way for a caller with measured sensitivity/domain evidence to prioritize dimensions while preserving the same bounds, hard gates, and evaluation ceiling.

### Proposed scope

Add an **optional deterministic coordinate order** to `FitConfig`.

Conceptually:

```python
FitConfig(
    max_evaluations=...,
    coordinate_order=(2, 0, 1),
)
```

Contract:

- omitted -> exact current index-order behavior;
- supplied value is a complete permutation of `0..N-1`;
- lower/upper direction order stays unchanged;
- max iterations/evaluations and plateau/oscillation semantics stay unchanged;
- Divine Eye hard-gate handling stays unchanged;
- resolved order is included in result JSON/provenance;
- malformed/incomplete/duplicate orders fail loud.

No replay engine, learned policy, model call, new dependency, or autonomous self-modification belongs in this upstream slice.

### Why / evidence plan

Downstream research is using recorded fit histories as replay worlds to learn coordinate priority, but the upstream primitive is useful independently: callers can prioritize known-sensitive parameters under expensive render budgets.

The PR should not claim real fidelity improvement until the downstream experiment has fresh paired evidence.

Required before upstream implementation is marked ready:

1. unit fixture where two coordinate orders under the same `max_evaluations` reach different best objective scores;
2. default/omitted order remains behavior-compatible;
3. malformed orders have field-specific errors;
4. real governed silhouette A/B evidence showing either:
   - higher clean silhouette IoU at equal render budget, or
   - same IoU within tolerance with fewer render evaluations;
5. no scale/aspect hard-gate regression.

Downstream RFC/prototype:
https://github.com/kvnloo/img2threejs/pull/15

### Availability

I can keep the upstream implementation to this primitive once the real-render evidence gate is satisfied.

## Summary / current state

This issue records a long-running, single-view, image-led procedural reconstruction and the workflow defects encountered. The model is **not complete** and has not passed the visual/CS2 gates.

![Loop 18 front render — latest reviewed render, not a final result](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef5f491f-4efc-4633-8f8d-217a53ccbe16)

The image above is the latest successfully captured *and reviewed* front render (loop 18), not loop 19. Loop 19's render capture timed out and has no verified screenshots or review scores.

- Pipeline state at last confirmed read: `blockout`, loop `19/20`, current step `render-capture`.
- Last reviewed result (loop 18): visual global score `0.59`; CS2 review `reject`; no pass advanced.
- Current correction budget: `19/20` total. Do not reset or extend it implicitly.

## Reconstruction metadata

- **Item:** `★ Huntsman Knife | Marble Fade (Factory New)`
- **Input:** `.img2threejs/evidence/reference-normalized.png`, 2560×1440; normalized from the supplied progressive JPEG to a pixel-identical PNG (pHash `16591510568606950641`). The reference shows one front/side view only.
- **CS2 metadata:** paint index `413`, rarity `Covert`, float range `0–0.08`; exact float and paint seed are unknown.
- **Geometry:** `agent-inferred`; no Huntsman-specific adapter was available. Hidden/rear geometry is not verified and must not be described as official/vanilla-accurate.
- **Surface:** de-lit 2048² orthographic atlas; projection is front-only. Edges, back and hole walls use unprojected material.
- **Agent:** Hermes Agent (Nous Research)
- **Model:** `openai/gpt-6-luna`
- **LLM provider:** OpenRouter
- **Visual review:** agent vision through `vision_analyze`; no separate external VLM model/version was exposed.
- **Build/runtime:** img2threejs `forge` + `plugin-cs2`, TypeScript/Three.js, Vite, Playwright with cached Chromium 1243.

The source is user-supplied and its rights/provenance have not been verified. The attachment is a reconstruction preview, not a rights-clearance claim; do not mark extracted Valve pixels rights-safe or commit them without verifying provenance.

## Steps completed

1. **Image analysis and admission:** decoded/normalized the reference, recorded conditional suitability because only one side is visible, and preserved the hidden-side limitation.
2. **CS2 intake:** classified the item, wrote the manifest/augmentation/assessment and recorded the image-only inference route; no Huntsman adapter match was guessed.
3. **Projection preparation:** solved the front camera pose, de-lit the reference and baked the front-only projection atlas with unseen regions left unprojected.
4. **Spec and inventory:** authored the object sculpt spec with 23 components, 45 blade stations, 32 feature links and 21 inventoried details; added 6 material definitions and PBR evidence. Strict-quality validation was iterated until it passed.
5. **Generation and Showcase wiring:** generated the Three.js factory, integrated it into the Huntsman Showcase preview and verified source/Showcase parity at multiple revisions.
6. **Deterministic/visual loop:** repeatedly captured front/orbit views; ran Tier‑1 silhouette/proportion, multi-angle, interior-difference, CS2 and agent-vision reviews only after their prerequisites passed. Hard Tier‑1 failures were not sent to VLM review.
7. **Loop 19 spec/build:** sampled the visible dark-handle tail through source rows 840–870, updated the profile to taper through y=860 and stop where the dark region disappears, and changed the visible front cap to source projection. Strict validation passed. The generator was forced, then the spec-backed custom projection hooks were restored from the saved pre-force artifact. Core and Showcase factories are identical (360,304 bytes; SHA-256 `e94a6b9ccf84eb861b50960289d617a437a767439d77f158442a5410c42b464a`). Vite production build passed (350 modules). `npm run build` still exits 2 on unrelated repository TypeScript diagnostics; there were 0 Huntsman diagnostics.

## Notable review history

| Loop | Change / result | Gate outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1–2 | Framing and organizing-mesh corrections. | Loop 2 Tier‑1 IoU `0.8666`, orbit gate passed; critical visual features still below threshold. |
| 3–5 | Rail/guard and material-mapping work; crossguard repositioned. | Loop 3 IoU `0.8753`, CS2 reject. Loop 4 VLM global `0.58`; critical `0.61/0.46/0.39/0.57`. Loop 5 VLM global `0.31`; critical `0.34/0.38/0.18/0.58`. |
| 7–11 | Tang-hole/ricasso measurements, blade-edge and profile refinements. | Loop 7 IoU `0.8551`, VLM global `0.48`; loop 8 IoU `0.8417` hard-failed; loop 9 VLM global `0.36`; loop 10 failed aspect delta (`0.0658`); loop 11 IoU `0.8427` hard-failed. No VLM review was run on the hard-failed loops. |
| 12–15 | Camera-only framing correction, grip bounds and front projection on visible ricasso/tang faces. | Loop 12 VLM global `0.44`; loop 14 Tier‑1 IoU `0.896`; loop 15 VLM global `0.52`, painted face `0.93`, CS2 reject. |
| 16–18 | Isolated and projected the dominant shoulder; extended the handle contour from measured pixels. | Loop 16 VLM global `0.57`, critical blade/edge/guard/grip `0.84/0.81/0.58/0.74`; loop 17 `0.59`, `0.84/0.81/0.62/0.76`; loop 18 Tier‑1 IoU `0.8992`, aspect `0.0253`, scale `0.0247`, orbit ratios `0.9083/0.8996/0.9946`, interior difference `0.18755`. Loop 18 VLM remained `0.59`; CS2 rejected `edge_curve`, `guard_quillon`, `grip_ring`. |
| 19 | Measured the dark tail at x=1488–1520 (y=840), x=1489–1514 (y=850), x=1494–1507 (y=860), with no dark run by y=870; tapered the handle contour and projected its front cap. | Strict spec validation and Vite build passed. **No verified render, Tier‑1, orbit, CS2 or VLM result yet.** |

Loop 18’s Tier‑1 and orbit passes do not imply visual acceptance. Blockout can continue only after a fresh loop 19 render is captured and reviewed; the visual target remains global ≥`0.70` and every critical feature ≥`0.82`.

## Workflow mistakes / failure handling

- **Generator overwrite:** `generate_threejs_factory.py --force` replaces hand-added projection helpers/UV grouping. This required restoring custom code after several forced regenerations. The spec carries the projection decision, but the generator still does not emit the complete custom implementation. Avoid treating a successful generation alone as the final source.
- **State/evidence drift:** build evidence was not marked immediately on an earlier resume, so `forge/next.py` still reported `build-current-pass` pending and the force generator was replayed. The step was later marked with evidence; the state then advanced to `render-capture`. Mark each successful gate immediately and re-read `next.py` before continuing.
- **Misaligned zoom evidence (loop 18):** a manually assembled zoom crop assumed a contain-style panel scale. `make_comparison_sheet.py` actually uses `resize_cover` with center cropping. The zoom image therefore was **not aligned** between reference and render; conclusions attributed to that crop are unreliable. The full comparison sheet is still usable as a macro view. Feature crops must be regenerated using the sheet’s actual crop transform or, preferably, a camera/world-to-screen mapping.
- **Capture timeout (loop 19):** a single Playwright command that waited for runtime and captured front plus three orbits timed out at 180 seconds without verified output. The preview URL returned HTTP 200, but that does not prove `window.__ready` or screenshot capture succeeded. Capture one view at a time, persist/hash each immediately, and record page errors/readiness.
- **Full build versus target bundle:** Vite-only build passes; `npm run build` fails on existing errors in `falchion-sapphire` (unused/implicit-any diagnostics) and `registry.ts:1437` (`Light[]` passed as `Object3D`). Keep those separate from Huntsman status and do not report the full build as passing.
- **Review scope:** visual scores are agent-vision judgments from a single side view, not an independent external VLM rating. Hidden/rear accuracy remains unverified.
- **Attachment upload:** a first GitHub asset upload returned an asset URL, but a pre-issue GET returned 404 before it was linked. A second upload URL is embedded above. The first unlinked asset may be orphaned; verify the embedded image after issue creation.

## Proposed workflow improvements / acceptance criteria

- [ ] Make projection restoration generator-supported (declarative spec extension or stable hook); add a test that a forced generation preserves the blade/tang/ricasso/shoulder/handle front projection and leaves hidden surfaces unprojected.
- [ ] Make state marking atomic/idempotent with build evidence so a resumed run does not unnecessarily re-run destructive `--force` generation after an already verified build.
- [ ] Add a feature-crop helper that reproduces `resize_cover` and camera projection exactly; validate landmark alignment before using a crop for visual scoring.
- [ ] Make browser capture resumable per view (front, orbit A/B, rear) with readiness, page-error output, persistent PNGs and hashes; a timeout must preserve successfully completed shots.
- [ ] Separate repository-wide TypeScript baseline failures from per-demo validation; fix or track unrelated Falchion/registry errors independently.
- [ ] Keep the CS2 rights/provenance flag explicit and do not claim official/vanilla or hidden-side fidelity.

## Next required action

Resume from the local state’s `render-capture` step: capture and verify loop 19 front/orbit screenshots individually, then run Tier‑1, multi-angle, interior-difference and pass gate. Only then run the loop 19 CS2 and agent-vision reviews, record exactly one correction action and sync the state. Do not advance from blockout on deterministic gates alone.

title: docs: add PLUGINS.md — installing and using plugins from the pipeline side
body:
## What

Two halves of one gap, docs only — 3 files, no code, no manifests, no test changes. Rebased onto the current main (`docs: clarify base skill and plugin quickstart`) and aligned with its harness setup (`npx --yes @img2threejs/img2@latest`, `img2 plugins`, short plugin ids on CLI >= 0.4.0).

1. **`docs/PLUGINS.md`** (new) — the pipeline's view of plugins: what a run in this repo actually sees, how a plugin's declarations reach this checklist, and what to check when a profile you expect is missing.
2. **`SKILL.md`** — the plugin check becomes **step zero**: a mandatory preflight ahead of the Core Promise, instead of a closing note plus a rule that said to stop and name an `img2 add` command.
3. **`README.md`** — one pointer to `docs/PLUGINS.md` where the plugin section ends, next to the `WRITING_A_PLUGIN.md` pointer.

## Why

The README says how to install a plugin and how to choose one. The harness `docs/PLUGIN_CONTRACT.md` states the normative rules. Neither says what a run in *this* repo actually sees.

The skill router had the mirror-image gap: it *described* the plugin surface near the bottom of the file, and its hard rule was to **stop** when `state.py init` named an unavailable profile. Both fail the same way — a missing domain gets discovered *after* the spec is authored, and setup is treated as a blocker rather than as step zero. A domain decides what a run can reach before its first script runs; that ordering is the whole point.

It is not hypothetical. On the machine this was written on: five plugins linked into a non-default `$IMG2_HOME`, one registered in the active one, and "I installed it" quietly meaning "this run cannot see it" — while the profile list, generated from the registry, said so plainly all along.

## `docs/PLUGINS.md` — what it covers

- **Three layers and the boundary**: the harness ships no domain capability; this pipeline consumes a plugin only as declared data, so installing or removing one can never change what this pipeline emits (floors raise-only, and the merge clamps).
- **Install / verify / remove**: harness setup through the npm package, `img2 plugins` catalog, `add` (`--ref`, `--link`, `--allow-any-source`, short ids vs the portable `img2threejs/plugin-<id>` form), `list`, `doctor`, `sync --check`, `remove` — why a `requires` mismatch **blocks** rather than warns, and that some plugins ship from private repositories.
- **What a run sees depends on `$IMG2_HOME`**: composition is the registry at `$IMG2_HOME/plugins.json`; this pipeline reads the registry and never globs `plugins/` (so an orphaned checkout of a removed plugin contributes nothing), plus the commands that answer the question for the environment in which they run.
- **How `domain.json` reaches the checklist**: `setupSteps`/`passSteps`/`rigSteps` anchoring, `{plugin_dir}` substitution at splice time, `specCollection`; plus the two things that bite — rows are `[stepId, command]` **pairs** with **no `actor` field**, and `domain.json` has a **different closed placeholder set** from `steps.json`/`gates.json` (`{plugin_dir}`, `{reference}`, `{spec}`, `{pass_id}`), because the pipeline renders it with `str.format()`, which raises on any other name. `{workspace}` is legal in `steps.json` and a run-time crash here; `doctor` refuses the wrong set and names the file's own valid set.
- **Loud failure modes**: a missing profile names what *is* installed; an unknown `domain.json` key is refused rather than ignored; two providers on one domain `id` raise rather than pick.
- **Plugin gates**: the verdict envelope, the exit-code contract, `gate_runner` aggregation with `stopped`/`skipped`, and where a plugin gate attaches to the review record.
- **Host skills**: the harness links `img2-<id>` for the hosts in its `HOSTS` table; what to do when your host is not listed (link it with the same name convention, or read the absolute paths the checklist already prints) — and that adding the host belongs **upstream in the harness**, not in a local patch.
- **Symptom → cause → action table**, and a "where to read next" map that keeps this page the pipeline's view while the contract stays the contract.

## `SKILL.md` — step zero

- New **"Preflight: check and install the plugin surface (before any work)"** section, ahead of the Core Promise: `img2 --version --json`, `img2 list`, `img2 doctor`, and the `state.py init --profile` choices; the rule that `$IMG2_HOME` decides what a run sees (a plugin installed into the inactive home is linked, audited, and contributes nothing; `img2 list` and the `--profile` choices must agree); and, when a domain plugin serves the item, **install it and confirm its profile appears before starting** — never silently downgrade to `generic`, never vendor the domain logic.
- The Core Promise names it: **step zero is the preflight above**.
- "The img2 harness" no longer says the skill "never installs anything itself … and stop". It vendors no domain logic and never writes a substitute for it, but installing is part of starting a run; only a plugin that genuinely does not exist upstream is a blocker to report.
- The "Domain plugin flows" subsection points at `docs/PLUGINS.md`.

## Verification

Read against an installed harness (`img2` 0.2.3, contract 14, coreApi 1) and by running, not by reading:

- `img2 --version --json`, `img2 list`, `img2 doctor`, `img2 doctor --json`, `img2 capabilities`
- `img2 add --link` against local plugin checkouts, and the registry / `receipts.json` they wrote
- `python3 forge/state.py init --help` under two different `$IMG2_HOME` values, confirming the profile list is registry-derived (`{generic, character, cs2}` vs `{generic, animated-character, character, cs2, environment}`) — the evidence behind the page's central claim
- `forge/_shared/domains/__init__.py` read line by line for the splice, validation and error behaviour the page states
- `plugin-cs2`'s `plugin.json` / `domain.json` / `steps.json` / `gates.json` used as the worked example

The version note in both files is checked against a real CLI: the 0.2.3 `commands[]` list is `install add remove list doctor sync capabilities` — no `plugins`, which is exactly why the page says short ids and `img2 plugins` need 0.4.0+.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The page restates no normative rule as its own: where it and the contract could disagree, it defers, and "read next" points at the contract rather than duplicating it.
- The `HOSTS`-table gap is stated as a harness-side gap with the real fix named, not worked around in prose.

- Optional component `hinge: {axisStart, axisEnd, restAngleDeg?}`; verify finite nondegenerate axes.

title: [Contribution]: probe lossless WebP and big-endian TIFF dimensions
body:
### What are you proposing?
A bounded existing-code fix (reference-image technical metadata probing, no runtime dependency).

### Target issue URL or number
New reproducible defect in `forge/stage1_intake/probe_image.py`; no matching open WebP/TIFF issue or PR appeared in the repository search.

### Reproduction
1. Probe a **lossless** WebP image using the `VP8L` chunk (for example the tiny real 1024×513 fixture in downstream PR [#44](https://github.com/kvnloo/img2threejs/pull/44)). `detect_image_type` says `webp`, but `webp_size` returns `None`, so a valid image gets `width=null, height=null` and `could not read image dimensions`. The current parser recognizes `VP8X` and lossy `VP8 ` only.
2. Probe a standard big-endian TIFF IFD with single inline `SHORT` ImageWidth=1024 and ImageLength=513 tags. TIFF stores the inline SHORT in the high 16 bits of the four-byte value slot, but `tiff_size` always masks the low 16 bits. Both dimensions become zero and the parser returns `None`. Little-endian SHORT and both LONG variants should still work.

### Proposed scope
- Parse `VP8L`'s 0x2f signature and packed 14-bit width/height; reject insufficient/bad header bytes and unsupported version bits (per [RFC 9649](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9649.html)).
- Read inline TIFF SHORT tags from the correct half-word according to byte order.
- Add a real pre-encoded lossless WebP fixture, malformed-header checks, and both byte orders of TIFF SHORT/LONG tags. Keep `forge/` stdlib-only.

### Downstream evidence
- Tested fork change: [kvnloo/img2threejs#44](https://github.com/kvnloo/img2threejs/pull/44).
- [CI run](https://github.com/kvnloo/img2threejs/actions/runs/39212704868): Python 3.10 and Node 18/22 jobs passed.
- This only fixes **technical dimension probing**; it makes no claim about downstream image decoding or reconstruction fidelity.

### Upstream coordination
Request maintainer triage/intent before opening any upstream implementation PR. Do not auto-close an existing issue.

title: [Bug]: pHash invents black cells for images smaller than its 32px grid
body:
## Reproduction

`forge/_shared/image_hash.py:to_grayscale_downsampled()` assigns each source pixel to just one 32×32 output bucket with `x * size // width`. When the source is smaller than the hash grid, most output buckets remain zero, although the image contains no black pixels. The DCT interprets this as real dark image structure.

Minimal stdlib check against the current main branch:

```python
from forge._shared.image_hash import phash_from_image, hamming

def half_image(side):
    return [(30,30,30,255) if x < side // 2 else (220,220,220,255)
            for y in range(side) for x in range(side)]

a = phash_from_image(16, 16, half_image(16))
b = phash_from_image(32, 32, half_image(32))
print(hamming(a, b))  # currently 27 out of 64
```

These scenes are geometrically identical. The 16×16 hash instead reflects 768 fabricated black buckets. This violates the module's stated scale invariance and risks misleading reference-admission/Divine Eye comparisons involving small crops.

## Expected / acceptance

- Small source images populate **every** target cell using a principled, deterministic resampler.
- Equivalent 16×16 and 32×32 patterns produce identical or near-identical pHashes.
- Normal images (both dimensions >= 32) preserve their existing hashes; persisted reference hashes must not silently change.
- Pure Python stdlib; focused tests for rectangular/1×1 sources and truncated payloads.
- No implied 3D fidelity improvement without a separate render A/B.

An isolated downstream implementation with CI evidence is available at [kvnloo/img2threejs#47](https://github.com/kvnloo/img2threejs/pull/47). **1,420 Python tests passed (64 skipped), Node 18/22 checks passed** on its head. I am not treating the contribution as assigned; maintainer triage is welcome.

title: [Bug]: cyclic component parent references can exhaust generator recursion
body:
## Reproduction

The validator checks that a component's `parent` ID exists, but does not check whether parent references form a cycle. The generator's `filter_components_for_pass()` used to resolve parents recursively, adding each ID to `included_ids` only *after* returning from its parent. A self-parent or mutual cycle therefore produces `RecursionError`; even a valid 1,800-deep hierarchy can exceed the interpreter's recursion limit.

Minimal reproduction on the current upstream `main` (Python 3.10+, standard library only):

```python
from forge.tests.test_attachment_does_not_override_primitive import spec_with
from forge.stage2_spec.validate_sculpt_spec import validate_spec
from forge.stage3_build.generate_threejs_factory import generate

spec = spec_with("box", "assembled-solid")
spec["componentTree"][1]["parent"] = "part"  # self-parent
print([msg for msg in validate_spec(spec)[0] if "parent" in msg])
# Current upstream: no parent-cycle validation error.
generate(spec, "blockout")  # RecursionError from parent inclusion
```

Also reproducible with `body.parent = "part"` while `part.parent = "body"` (two-node cycle), or 1,800 valid reverse-ordered nested components (recursive stack exhaustion).

## Expected outcome

- Strict validation rejects self-parent and longer parent cycles with an explicit, actionable component chain.
- Direct generator entry points fail with a bounded, meaningful exception rather than unbounded recursion, including when callers bypass spec validation.
- Forward parent references remain **valid**. They already work and should not be rejected.
- Valid parent-first specs produce the same component emission order; no production dependencies introduced.

## Focused downstream evidence

[Downstream draft PR #54](https://github.com/kvnloo/img2threejs/pull/54) uses an iterative parent-chain walk and adds nine focused tests, including 100 seeded acyclic DAGs checked against the previous emission order and the 1,800-component valid chain.

[Verified fork CI](https://github.com/kvnloo/img2threejs/actions/runs/39376737906): **1,425 Python tests passed (64 skipped)**, plus Node 18/22 checks. Draft only; **please triage scope before any upstream PR**. The work is unrelated to parent-local hinge issue #118 and can be reviewed independently.

- `scripts/ci/showcase_table.py` (stdlib): reads the gallery's `demos.json`, renders the 12 newest demos with `status: final` (gallery order) between `<!-- showcase:start/end -->`. title: Agents can bypass forge/state.py by editing .img2threejs/state.json directly
body:
## Problem

`forge/state.py` is the documented only way to move the checklist (`SKILL.md:142-148`: "`.img2threejs/state.json` is the local checklist authority"). `forge/_shared/workflow_state.py:312` `mark_steps` enforces order (`out-of-order checklist update`) and evidence (`completing a mandatory step requires at least one --evidence value`). But those rules only hold when the agent goes through `state.py`. `state.json` is a plain file in the job directory, so an agent can rewrite it and skip both checks.

## Observed (playground stg, 2026-10-22)

Run `66e4adb1-88e9-4111-b0bf-6d01bb542ccc` ("Kukri Knife", pi + MiniMax M3, core checkout `ae365d4` mounted read-only):

- Near the end the agent ran Python that loaded `state.json`, set each checklist entry's `status` directly, ran a script commented "Re-mark every step", and set `d['currentPass']='complete'` directly.
- The runner's step events over the same 47 seconds: 18/23 done → 20/23 → 12/23 (`build-current-pass`) → 18/23 → `complete` 20/23.
- The final state has 20 `done` (each with evidence) and 3 `skipped`, and the run reported `quality: complete`.
- Whether any gate was actually skipped cannot be told after the fact: the playground's run log dropped those multi-line commands (img2threejs/playground#145), and `state.json` keeps no history.

## Proposal

Make a direct edit detectable, since it cannot be prevented while the agent can write its job directory:

1. `state.py` appends each transition (step, status, evidence, time) to an append-only log beside `state.json`, with each entry chaining the hash of the previous one and of the resulting `state.json`.
2. `next.py` (and a new `state.py verify`) refuses to continue, or reports `tampered`, when `state.json` does not match the last chained entry. `currentPass` / `currentStep` are derived only by `recompute`, never trusted from the file.
3. The final result marks a run whose state was edited outside `state.py` as not `complete`.

The runner side (recording such writes, #145) is detection only. This issue is the enforcement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Editing `state.json` by hand (any field) makes `next.py` / `state.py verify` report tampering and refuse to advance.
- [ ] A run driven only through `state.py` verifies cleanly.
- [ ] Existing state files without a transition log get a clear one-time migration message, not a crash.

title: fix(gates): honour textureless at material-pass; stop self-intersection false positives on surface-net meshes
body:
> Filed by Naren's AI agent (Claude Code), from a stylized-fox build that hit both bugs.

## Summary

Two gate bugs, each with a regression test that fails before the fix.

### 1. `material-pass` ignores the `textureless` declaration

**Symptom.** A spec whose materials declare `textureless: {declared: true, evidence: [...]}` passes
`validate_sculpt_spec.py --strict-quality`, but `orchestrate_passes.py check --pass-id material-pass`
reports 7 quality-first gaps per such material (textureResolution, textureProjection, frequency
bands, roughness map, height/normal, AO, referencePbr). The generator refuses the pass for the same
reason, so the build can never pass material-pass.

**Root cause.** `validate_look_dev_targets` skips the quality-first texture bar for
`qualityTier == "utility"` **or** `is_textureless(material)`. `material_pass_gaps` in
`orchestrate_passes.py` only skips `utility`. The only way through is relabelling a hero material
`utility`, which `validate_textureless`'s own docstring calls dishonest.

### 2. `self_intersection.py` reports clean surface-net meshes as folded

**Symptom.** On a clean fox built from implicit-SDF surface nets, the gate flagged 295/1968 sampled
vertices "inside" (cape shell 161/393). A generalized winding number found 0 folds.

**Root cause: two independent bugs, and neither is ray hits on shared edges.** Hits on shared
edges and vertices were already returned as *undecided*, never as inside.

1. **Centroid fallback normals.** The mesh dump had no `normals`, so every sample was stepped along
   `vertex − centroid`. That is outward only on a star-shaped mesh. On a cape shell, a curled tail
   or a torus it points *into* the solid for the whole inner side, so those samples really were
   inside: correct parity on the wrong point. All 295 fox flags had `normalSource: "centroid"`.
   With area-weighted face normals the same meshes give 1 flag.
2. **Masking the sample's incident triangles.** That last flag (head) has winding number 0 at the
   stepped point. Two of its three rays legitimately *enter* through a triangle incident to the
   sample vertex (concave crease) and exit further on. The gate masked incident triangles, dropped
   the entry, kept the exit, and got odd parity. The mask dates from when rays could point inward.
   Rays are now cast into the outward hemisphere from a point `epsilon` off the surface, so a hit on
   the sample's own neighbourhood is a real crossing.

## Changes

- `forge/stage3_build/orchestrate_passes.py`: `material_pass_gaps` imports and applies the
  validator's own `is_textureless`, so the two gates share one predicate and cannot drift again.
  (`generate_threejs_factory.py` already imports from `stage2_spec` the same way. The validator is
  stdlib-only, ~11 ms to import, and there is no import cycle.)
- `forge/stage4_review/self_intersection.py`:
  - No supplied normals → area-weighted face normals (welded by position as before), oriented
    outward by the mesh's signed volume. `normalSource` reports `"faceNormals"` instead of
    `"centroid"`. A malformed supplied normal falls back to the face normal. A vertex with no live
    triangle is *undecided*, never guessed.
  - Incident-triangle masking removed (`_count_crossings` loses its `excluded` parameter).
- `forge/tests/test_textureless_material.py`: new `MaterialPassGate` class. A declared material
  yields no material-pass gaps; an undeclared sibling in the same spec still does.
- `forge/tests/test_self_intersection.py`: a ~50-line naive surface-net fixture mirroring the
  emitted `polygonizeSdf` (quad-split triangulation, gradient normals), and a new
  `SurfaceNetFalsePositives` class:
  - a torus with no normals is clean (before: 110/456 flagged);
  - a hard-`min` two-sphere crease with exact gradient normals is clean (before: 4 flagged);
  - negative control: the torus with its top pushed through its underside is still caught.

  Plus `test_inward_wound_mesh_without_normals_is_still_clean`, which guards the signed-volume
  orientation. Two existing tests that pinned `normalSource == "centroid"` now expect
  `"faceNormals"`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: a `### Fixed` entry for both fixes under `[Unreleased]`.

## Description matches the diff

- [x] The title and summary describe exactly what the diff changes (no unrelated files, no commits inherited from another PR). `docs:` PRs touch only docs; CI enforces this.

  The diff is the 5 files above. The branch also carries a merge of `main` (`954cd58`) to resolve a
  `CHANGELOG.md` conflict; it adds no files to the diff.

## Verified

Run locally on Python 3.14.4, branch head `8a1c82e`.

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s forge/tests
Ran 1422 tests in 39.255s
OK (skipped=63)

$ python3 forge/tests/test_pipeline.py
Ran 57 tests in 11.956s
OK
```

Each new test failed on `6e60b5e` before the fix: `MaterialPassGate` (both tests), the torus
(110/456 flagged), the crease (4 flagged), and the `faceNormals` assertions.

Fox build, `self_intersection.py meshes.json --max-samples 400` (the mesh dump has no normals):

| mesh | before (`6e60b5e`) | after |
|---|---|---|
| Torso, legs and feet | 18 inside | 0 |
| Head | 9 | 0 |
| Tail | 29 | 0 |
| Cape shell | 161 | 0 |
| Cape collar | 78 | 0 |
| verdict | `SELF-INTERSECTION DETECTED`, exit 1 | `no self-intersection`, exit 0 |

At the default 4000-sample budget (16,551 samples) the result is 0 inside, with 182 undecided (1.1%).
At the 400-sample budget the undecided count is 16/1968 after vs 15/1968 before, so removing the mask
did not trade false positives for abstentions.

Generalized winding number at the stepped sample point:
- below 0.5 (outside) at all 506 vertices of the crease fixture, so the old gate's 4 flags there
  were false;
- 0 at the fox head vertex that survived the normals fix;
- 1.0 at the only two flags the fixed gate still raised in a sweep of 72 two-sphere unions, so those
  are real surface-net folds at a sharp crease.

Fox spec (20 materials, all declared textureless, `qualityPriority: reference-fidelity`):
- `material_pass_gaps`: **140 gaps before, 0 after**;
- `orchestrate_passes.py check --pass-id material-pass` now stops only at its normal next step:
  `Tier 1 diagnostics have not passed for this render`;
- `generate_threejs_factory.py --pass-id material-pass`: before, exit 2 (`needs spec refinement`);
  after, exit 0;
- generated code is unchanged: `--pass-id feature-placement` hashes identically before and after
  (`78cd8b57…`). The unlocked `material-pass` output differs from it only in the
  `// Sculpt build pass:` comment line.

Upstream's docs-quality checks, run locally against `origin/main`:

```
$ python3 scripts/ci/pr_scope.py --title "<this PR's title>" --base origin/main
type='fix' files=5 -> ok
$ python3 scripts/ci/md_tables.py --base origin/main                                  # exit 0
$ python3 scripts/ci/md_links.py --baseline scripts/ci/link-baseline.txt --base origin/main   # exit 0
$ python3 scripts/ci/skill_budget.py
SKILL.md: 4296 words (budget 4300)
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/ci/tests
Ran 23 tests ... OK
```

## Unverified claims

- **Python 3.10 (CI's version) was not run locally.** Everything above ran on 3.14.4.
- **The fox figures need artifacts not in this PR.** The numbers come from a local build whose
  `meshes.json` and spec are not attached. The in-repo tests reproduce both mechanisms on synthetic
  surface nets instead.
- **The showcase TypeScript typecheck gates were skipped** (no `IMG2THREEJS_SHOWCASE_ROOT`). Generated
  code is byte-identical for an existing pass, so they are not expected to change, but that is not
  re-proven.
- **`npm test` / `npm run package:check` (the CLI job) were not run.** The diff touches neither `bin/`
  nor `package.json`.
- **Agreement between the fixed ray parity and the winding number is only checked at the points
  listed under Verified.** That is not a proof for all meshes.
- **A mesh whose components are wound in opposite directions is untested.** Orientation is one global
  signed-volume sign; that limit is noted in a code comment.

## Validation

- [x] `python3 forge/tests/test_pipeline.py`: 57 tests OK.
- [x] Relevant targeted validation or test: `test_self_intersection` and `test_textureless_material`
  (51 tests OK); the full `forge/tests` suite (1422 OK, 63 skipped).
- [ ] Render or comparison-sheet review, if applicable: not applicable. No reconstruction output
  changes (generated code is byte-identical, see Verified).

## Contributor checklist

- [x] This PR keeps the code-only procedural reconstruction contract; it does not silently download meshes or art packs.
- [x] Existing object specs remain valid, or this PR documents the intentional compatibility change.
  There is no schema change. The intentional change is in report output: `self_intersection`
  reports `normalSource: "faceNormals"` instead of `"centroid"` when normals are absent (noted in
  `CHANGELOG.md`).
- [x] I added or updated tests for new gates, schema fields, or templates where applicable.
- [x] I updated documentation and roadmap status where applicable. `CHANGELOG.md` is updated. No
  roadmap item changes status, and no other doc described the centroid fallback.

title: fix(generator): reject cyclic component parent hierarchy and prevent recursion exhaustion
body:
## Summary

When component parent references form a cycle (self-parent or mutual cycles), the generator recursion in `filter_components_for_pass()` previously resulted in a `RecursionError`. In addition, deeply nested hierarchies (e.g. >1000 levels) could exceed the Python call stack limit.

This PR introduces cycle detection during spec validation and replaces recursive parent resolution in the generator with an iterative chain traversal that raises a clear `ValueError` if an invalid cyclic structure bypasses validation.

Refs #172

## Changes

- `forge/stage2_spec/validate_sculpt_spec.py`: Added parent reference cycle detection in `validate_components()`, outputting the specific component cycle chain.
- `forge/stage3_build/generate_threejs_factory.py`: Refactored `filter_components_for_pass()` to resolve ancestor dependencies iteratively, eliminating call stack exhaustion and raising `ValueError` on cyclic hierarchies.
- `forge/tests/test_cyclic_component_hierarchy.py`: Added 5 unit tests covering self-parent cycles, two-node cycles, generator cycle exceptions, deep hierarchies (1200+ components), and forward-reference preservation.

title: fix(forge): quality and robustness fixes across intake, spec, build, and review stages
body:
## Summary

This PR resolves several discrete defects and robustness issues across the intake, spec authoring, build generation, and review stages:

1. **Intake stream encoding (fixes #107 / #139):** Configures stdout/stderr error handling to `backslashreplace` in `search_specs.py` so searches containing bilingual cues (e.g. Vietnamese and Chinese terms) execute without `UnicodeEncodeError` on non-UTF-8 consoles.
2. **Explicit UTF-8 file operations (fixes #107 latent defects):** Adds explicit `encoding="utf-8"` to text reading and writing calls across `scalp_exposure.py`, `hair_gate.py`, `pairwise_penetration.py`, `joint_loops.py`, `self_intersection.py`, `geodesic_skinning.py`, `decimate.py`, `visual_hull.py`, `uv_unwrap.py`, and `morph_targets.py`.
3. **Region ID path traversal sanitization (fixes #103 / #151):** Sanitizes `regionId` in `material_region_analysis.py` to prevent directory traversal via backslashes or relative sequences (`..`), verifying that crops and PBR directories resolve strictly within the designated output directory.
4. **Sub-grid pHash downsampling (fixes #171):** Resamples grid cells from nearest source pixels in `to_grayscale_downsampled` when image dimensions are smaller than the 32px grid, eliminating artificial black bucket creation and restoring scale invariance between 16px and 32px crops.
5. **Lossless WebP and big-endian TIFF probing (fixes #170):** Adds `VP8L` header parsing for 14-bit packed dimensions per RFC 9649, and fixes big-endian TIFF inline 16-bit `SHORT` tag value extraction.
6. **Authored dimensions with identity scale (fixes #108):** In `scale_vector`, allows authored `dimensions` to take precedence when a scaffolded component carries an unedited `[1, 1, 1]` scale.
7. **Documentation clarity (fixes #150):** Clarifies architecture and artifact references in `README.md`.
8. **Workflow state resume (fixes #85):** Adds a `resume` command to `state.py` to allow re-opening passes during iterative refinement without losing checklist state.
9. **Curve-sweep attachment preservation (fixes #111):** Ensures components with authored `curveSweep` or `tubePath` descriptors preserve their swept geometry rather than collapsing into endpoint-derived cylinders.
10. **Consolidated test coverage:** Adds cross-module regression coverage in `forge/tests/test_forge_robustness.py`.

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest forge/tests/test_search_specs.py` (39/39 tests passed)
- `python3 -m unittest forge/tests/test_reference_admission.py` (11/11 tests passed)

title: [Contribution]: Optional rounded bevel for extrude profiles
body:
### What are you proposing?

A bounded new fix

### Target issue URL or number

new bounded fix

### Proposed scope

`buildExtrudeGeometry` hard-codes `bevelEnabled: false`, so every extruded part of a hard-surface subject (a device shell, a key, a panel) has razor edges. CONTRIBUTING lists generator bevels as a good first area.

Proposal: an optional `profile2D.bevel` `{size, thickness?, segments?}`. When present, the edges are rounded inside the authored envelope: the profile points stay the outer silhouette (`bevelOffset: -size`) and the caps stay at `0..depth` (inner depth shortened by `2 * thickness`, then translated). Without the field the emitted geometry is unchanged.

Intentionally left out: validator rules and schema docs for the new field (can follow in a separate PR if you want the feature).

### Acceptance criteria and validation plan

- An extrude with `profile2D.bevel` emits the bevel branch; an extrude without it emits no bevel code (new `forge/tests/test_extrude_bevel.py`).
- The new test fails against current main and passes with the change.
- Full suite stays green: `python3 -m unittest discover -s forge/tests` on Python 3.10 and 3.13, plus `python3 forge/tests/test_pipeline.py`.
- Visual check: used on 60+ extruded parts of a cassette-player reconstruction rendered with three.js 0.170.

### Availability

The implementation is ready on my fork (inforobotvit/img2threejs, branch feat/extrude-bevel), one commit with a test. I can open the PR right after this issue and adjust it based on review. Prepared with the help of Claude (Anthropic) and reviewed by me.
